articles.title: Monoclonal Antibodies for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Infants and Children: An Updated Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Motivated by the emergence of a long-acting monoclonal antibody (clesrovimab), the availability of data from the complete MELODY trial cohort, and results from a large randomized trial (HARMONIE), we updated our prior network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants. METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials that examined the efficacy and safety of RSV infection prophylaxis with clesrovimab, motavizumab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, and suptavumab versus one another or placebo or no prophylaxis in infants. We performed a frequentist framework random-effects network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Developments and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Eighteen trials enrolling 33,283 infants were included. Clesrovimab (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.02-0.37, moderate certainty), motavizumab (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.07-0.19, moderate certainty), and nirsevimab (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.34; moderate certainty) were associated with reductions in the rate of severe respiratory syncytial virus infection. Nirsevimab, motavizumab, clesrovimab, and intramuscular palivizumab were associated with reductions in RSV infection, and several agents were also associated with reduced hospitalization. Motavizumab and nirsevimab, and clesrovimab were associated with reductions in broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes. Motavizumab reduced both mechanical ventilation use and intensive care unit admission. No significant differences were found in all-cause mortality and drug-related or serious adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: This updated network meta-analysis confirmed that the effectiveness and safety of clesrovimab were comparable to those of established monoclonal antibodies. Motavizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab showed benefits for broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes.

articles.title: Fatigue in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: The Role of Drug Therapy Within a Holistic Management Framework.
articles.abstract: Fatigue is one of the most common and disabling symptoms experienced by individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Significant fatigue is experienced by approximately 40-80% of adults with IBD, with higher prevalence during active disease states but persisting in up to one-third of individuals who are in clinical remission. Fatigue is not solely a consequence of disease activity, but rather a unique and multifactorial manifestation of IBD. In this narrative review we synthesize evidence on the various mechanisms of fatigue in IBD, as well as pharmacological agents to address fatigue both directly or through secondary contributors including anaemia, psychiatric comorbidities, sleep disturbance, and pain. The review further situates pharmacological therapy within a holistic framework that integrates non-pharmacological approaches as part of a multidisciplinary approach to fatigue in IBD. Drug therapy has a meaningful role in this context, both when targeting disease-related inflammation and secondary contributors to fatigue. However, the evidence base for most of these approaches remains weak. It is clear that no single pharmacological agent will resolve IBD-related fatigue in isolation, but effective management should identify a patient's dominant contributors and address them systematically with both drug and nondrug intervention strategies. This framework should be delivered by a multidisciplinary team through an integrated care approach and optimally be guided by the patient's priorities and goals.

articles.title: Advancing Pregnancy and Pediatric Science through the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network.
articles.abstract: Human gestation is characterized by dynamic changes in maternal physiology and maturation of tissue functions before and after birth. The fetus and neonate are highly dependent upon transfer of maternal nutrients via the placenta and lactating mammary gland, which frequently involve selective membrane transporter proteins. At the same time, developmental changes in fetal and infant transport mechanisms critical for regulating absorption at the intestinal and blood-brain barriers are occurring. Coordinate regulation of cellular entry and efflux of nutrients, supplements, and xenobiotics, including drugs and environmental chemicals, must occur during this critical developmental period. In 2023, the National Institutes of Health launched the Transporter Elucidation Network (TEN) across four centers. This initiative applies experimental, computational, and translational approaches to (1) identify SoLute Carrier (SLC) superfamily and ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters in the human placenta, mammary gland, as well as the pediatric brain and intestinal barriers and, (2) characterize their localization, expression, function, and regulation. The Network seeks to identify functional determinants of transporters as gatekeepers of entry to placenta, mammary gland and brain, and applies structural biology, proteomics, metabolomics, organoids, liquid biopsies, and microphysiological systems to this end. Computational strategies, such as machine learning, virtual screening, physiologically based pharmacokinetics, and perinatal epidemiology complement our experimental approaches. This paper highlights the TEN's multidisciplinary strategies to address current challenges in perinatal and pediatric transporter research and its commitment to advancing state-of-the-art tools and new approach methodologies to fill critical gaps in our understanding of nutrient and xenobiotic exposure during early human development.

articles.title: Toward a Platform PBPK Model to Characterize the Plasma and Tissue Disposition of Unconjugated Antisense Oligonucleotides and GalNAc-Conjugated Small Interfering RNAs in Preclinical Species and Human.
articles.abstract: Unconjugated antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) and GalNAc-conjugated small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) have emerged as transformative therapeutic modalities, but their translation remains hindered by complex pharmacokinetics characterized by rapid plasma clearance, heterogeneous tissue uptake, and prolonged intracellular retention. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling offers a mechanistic framework to integrate these processes across species, yet applications to oligonucleotides remain limited, and existing efforts are typically restricted to specific chemistries or routes of administration. This study aimed to develop a cross-species PBPK platform to characterize the plasma and tissue disposition of unconjugated ASOs and GalNAc-siRNAs in preclinical species and humans, and to evaluate the consistency of estimated drug-specific parameters with pre-specified allometric scaling relationships within the domain of compounds and routes considered. Published datasets spanning mice, rats, non-human primates, and humans were integrated for representative unconjugated ASOs (Malat-1, GluR1, p-tau, tominersen) and GalNAc-siRNAs (ALN-AT3, givosiran, fitusiran). The PBPK model incorporated 11 tissue compartments, cerebrospinal fluid substructures, tissue substructures, endosomal trafficking, non-specific binding in kidney and liver, and ASGPR-mediated internalization for GalNAc-siRNAs. Parameters for endocytosis, exocytosis, and degradation were estimated, and estimated values were compared with pre-specified allometric exponents to assess physiological plausibility (i.e., as a consistency check rather than independent inference of scaling laws). The model captured plasma, liver, kidney, and CNS profiles across species, reproducing rapid systemic clearance with prolonged tissue half-lives. Estimated parameter values for endocytosis, exocytosis, and non-specific kidney binding were consistent with pre-specified allometric exponents (b = -0.25 and -0.2, respectively), supporting the physiological plausibility of the estimates. Sensitivity analyses identified endocytosis and rate of degradation as dominant determinants of systemic and tissue disposition. This work establishes a translational PBPK platform for unconjugated ASOs and GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs, enabling quantitative interspecies extrapolation within the domain of the compounds, routes, and species studied. The framework provides a mechanistic basis to support dose selection, safety assessment, and clinical translation for these subclasses; extrapolation to other oligonucleotide subclasses (e.g., GalNAc-ASOs, unconjugated siRNAs, LNP-formulated oligonucleotides) will require additional datasets and dedicated validation.

articles.title: A PTPRO inhibitor Pi mitigates endotoxemia-induced encephalopathy-mediated blood-brain barrier disruption through cytoskeletal regulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Septic encephalopathy (SE) is closely associated with disruption of blood-brain barrier (BBB), resulting in neurological deficits and poor clinical outcomes. Protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO) regulates disease states by dephosphorylating membrane-associated proteins and modulating intracellular signalling. Here we have examined the role of PTPRO in regulating BBB permeability and have assessed a PTPRO inhibitor (Pi) in mitigating BBB disruption during endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Genetic and pharmacological approaches, including PTPRO overexpression, knockdown or deficiency and Pi treatment, were used to evaluate endothelial dysfunction in bEND.3 cells, primary mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells and an LPS-induced murine model of endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy. Barrier dysfunction, cytoskeletal remodelling and signalling events were assessed using permeability assays, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence and in vivo BBB leakage analyses. KEY RESULTS: LPS increased PTPRO expression in brain tissue from endotoxemic mice and cerebral endothelial cells. Elevated PTPRO promoted F-actin reorganization, stress fibre formation and intercellular gap formation, whereas Pi treatment or PTPRO silencing attenuated these changes. PTPRO overexpression worsened endothelial barrier dysfunction, while Pi reduced thrombin-induced permeability in bEND.3 cells and wild-type primary endothelial cells. Primary endothelial cells from PTPRO-deficient mice were protected. Mechanistically, PTPRO regulated cytoskeletal dynamics through the ErbB2-Rho-MLC2 pathway. In vivo, Pi treatment and PTPRO deficiency reduced BBB leakage, with limited effects on inflammatory cytokines. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: These findings identify PTPRO as an important regulator of BBB disruption in endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy and support pharmacological targeting of PTPRO as a potential strategy for preserving sepsis-associated BBB injury.

articles.title: N-nitroso-hydrochlorothiazide: in vivo mutagenicity evaluation in a transgenic rodent model.
articles.abstract: N-nitrosamine drug substance related impurities (NDSRIs) are considered to be within the "cohort of concern" (CoC) due to their potential mutagenic carcinogenicity. However, increasing evidence indicates variability in mutagenic potency across this class. N-nitroso-hydrochlorothiazide (N-nitroso-HCTZ), an impurity associated with hydrochlorothiazide, has shown positive results in bacterial mutagenicity (Ames) assays, although mechanistic studies suggest these findings are likely driven by reactive degradation products rather than the parent compound. To further characterize mutagenic potential in vivo, a transgenic rodent (TGR) gene mutation assay was conducted in the Muta™Mouse test system. Male mice were administered N-nitroso-HCTZ by oral gavage at 0, 18.5, 55.7, 167, 500, or 750 mg/kg/day for 28 consecutive days. Mutant frequency (lacZ) was evaluated in liver and glandular stomach at 167, 500, and 750 mg/kg/day. Systemic exposure was confirmed in a toxicokinetic study following a single 750 mg/kg dose. N-nitroso-HCTZ was well tolerated, and no statistically significant increases in mutant frequency were observed in either tissue at any evaluated dose. All values were within historical control ranges, while the positive control demonstrated the anticipated response. Under the conditions of this study, N-nitroso-HCTZ did not induce gene mutations in vivo.

articles.title: One year of Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers.
FGF21-NR1D1 Signaling Restrains the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 Axis to Counteract Integrated Renal-Vascular Injury in Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Hypertension leads to concomitant injuries in the kidney and vasculature, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this coordinated pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify activation of the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 axis as being associated with coordinated renal and vascular injury in hypertension. In hypertension, this pathway was concurrently activated in the liver, kidney, and vasculature and was associated with renal fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, and oxidative stress. Pharmacological inhibition of CYP4A attenuated these pathological changes, supporting a functional contribution of this axis to hypertensive organ injury. Genetic and pharmacological evidence further demonstrated that FGF21 acts as an endogenous negative regulator of CYP4A/20-HETE signaling. Mechanistically, FGF21 restored expression of the nuclear receptor NR1D1, which was suppressed under hypertensive conditions, and this effect was associated with reduced CYP4A expression independently of ERK1/2 signaling. The functional relevance of the FGF21-NR1D1 axis was supported by the observation that NR1D1 antagonism largely abolished the protective effects of FGF21. Thus, these findings elucidate a mechanistic axis linking FGF21-NR1D1 signaling to the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 pathway and suggest that modulation of this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for hypertensive renal and vascular injury.

articles.title: Hierarchically sequential targeting nanoplatform suppresses NETosis-promoted angiogenesis for corneal neovascularization therapy.
articles.abstract: Corneal neovascularization (CorNV) lacks effective therapies due to poor drug delivery and a complex inflammatory microenvironment, necessitating a deeper understanding of the underlying pathogenic mechanisms and the development of efficient delivery systems. Here we show that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are pathologically activated in CorNV and identify peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) as a key therapeutic target. To achieve coordinated inhibition of NETosis and downstream vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, we engineer a reactive oxygen species (ROS) responsive copolymer encapsulating the PAD4 inhibitor Cl-amidine (Ca@PNH) that hierarchically targets neovascular endothelial cells and activated neutrophils via HRH and neutrophil elastase binding peptide (NEBP) peptides. Upon topical administration, Ca@PNH achieves prolonged ocular retention and lesion specific ROS triggered drug release, suppressing both NETs formation and angiogenesis. In a mouse CorNV model, this spatiotemporal strategy effectively treats neovascularization with excellent safety. Collectively, our work systematically establishes NETs as critical drivers of CorNV, identifies PAD4 as a druggable target, and offers a hierarchical delivery paradigm for inflammation driven ocular diseases.

articles.title: Bushen Huoxue Formula promotes osteoporotic fracture healing by CGRP-mediated dual regulation of BMSCs-osteoclasts balance through modulating mitochondrial energy metabolism.
articles.abstract: Osteoporotic fracture (OPF) is a serious complication that severely impairs the quality of life. Bushen Huoxue Formula (BHF), a clinically established prescription based on the TCM principle of "tonifying the kidney and activating blood circulation," has been widely used to treat osteoporosis. However, its efficacy in OPF and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, using a rat OPF model, we found that BHF treatment significantly accelerated the fracture healing process and improved callus microstructure and mineralization. Multi-omics analysis revealed that its therapeutic effect was closely associated with the regulation of mitochondrial energy metabolism, identifying CGRP as a key differential target. Mechanistically, CGRP was upregulated in bone mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), where it enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism and promoted osteogenic differentiation. Conversely, in osteoclast precursor RAW264.7 cells, CGRP was downregulated and inhibited osteoclast differentiation, demonstrating its dual regulatory role in bone remodeling via the same target. Further studies showed that taurine, a major component of BHF, could recapitulate the formula's effects by modulating CGRP to promote osteogenesis and suppress osteoclastogenesis. Importantly, corroborative clinical research demonstrated that BHF treatment effectively alleviated clinical symptoms and promoted fracture repair in OPF patients. In summary, BHF facilitates OPF healing through CGRP mediated mitochondrial energy metabolism, providing both mechanistic insight and clinical evidence for its repositioning from osteoporosis to fracture management.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into the therapeutic effects of Mongolian medicine Eligengurigumu-7 against non-alcoholic fatty liver disease via the PPAR signalling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)， is characterised by a complex, multi-stage pathogenesis and progression and imposes a substantial economic burden on global public health. Thus, an urgent need exists to improve the understanding of NAFLD-related hepatic disease progression and identify effective therapeutic strategies. Eligengurigumu-7 (GRGM-7) is a common treatment prescription for liver diseases in Mongolian medicine. However, its pharmacodynamics and mechanism of action remain largely unclear. PURPOSE: To evaluate the hepatoprotective efficacy of GRGM-7 against NAFLD, identify its bioactive constituents absorbed into the bloodstream, and elucidate its key molecular targets and underlying regulatory pathways. METHODS: The key differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and pathways during the progression of NAFLD-related hepatic diseases were identified through bioinformatics analysis and immunofluorescence validation of clinical samples. NAFLD mouse models induced with either a high-fat diet (HFD) or a methionine- and choline-deficient diet (MCD) were established. The therapeutic effects of GRGM-7 against NAFLD were evaluated in these models by comparing the physiological, biochemical, and pathological indicators of the control groups, model groups, and each dose treatment group. Through RNA-sequencing and non-targeted metabolomics analysis and the combined analysis of multi-source datasets, the key pharmacodynamic targets, regulatory function directions, and regulatory pathways of GRGM-7 involved in improving NAFLD were identified and verified through reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting (WB) experiments. The chemical components of GRGM-7 were identified using ultra performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), and the compounds absorbed into the bloodstream (CABs) were identified and analysed based on the principles of serum pharmacochemistry. CABs were quantitatively analysed in the original herbal formulation through high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and molecular docking was used to analyse the interaction between the CABs and active targets. The hepatoprotective effects of CABs and GRGM-7, as well as their effects on the targets were confirmed in an in vitro NAFLD model of oleic acid-induced AML-12 cells. Additionally, PPARγ and ACLY were subjected to siRNA-mediated silencing, and fenofibrate was used as a pharmacological agonist of PPARα to further functionally validate the involvement of the PPAR signaling pathway and ACLY in the effects of GRGM-7. RESULTS: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signalling was a crucial pathway involved in NAFLD-related hepatic disease progression. GRGM-7 administration ameliorated MCD- and HFD-induced NAFLD in mice and protected the liver by regulating the PPAR signalling pathway, promoting fatty acid metabolism, and maintaining liver lipid homeostasis. ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) served as a key candidate target associated with the progression of NAFLD and therapeutic action of GRGM-7. GRGM-7 contained several chemical components that were absorbed into the bloodstream. Among these CABs, cosmosiin exhibited a high affinity for key DEGs and crucial targets within signalling pathways. Moreover, cosmosiin showed a favourable hepatoprotective effect on the NAFLD cell model induced in vitro. GRGM-7 exhibited the strongest hepatoprotective effect in vitro, accompanied by modulation of the PPAR signalling pathway. Silencing of ACLY or PPARγ alleviated metabolic abnormalities, whereas subsequent GRGM-7 treatment produced further improvements. Fenofibrate treatment similarly ameliorated the OA-induced metabolic abnormalities, whereas combined treatment with fenofibrate and GRGM-7 further enhanced these effects, supporting the involvement of the PPAR signalling pathway and ACLY in the metabolic effects of GRGM-7. CONCLUSION: PPAR signalling was the key pathway involved in the progression of NAFLD-related hepatic diseases, and ACLY was one of the key potential targets. GRGM-7 regulated the PPAR signalling pathway by modulating fatty acid metabolism, thereby exerting a hepatoprotective effect. These findings highlight the potential utility of GRGM-7 as a therapeutic agent for NAFLD.

articles.title: Zuojin Wan reverses cetuximab resistance in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer via the NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ axes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cetuximab (CET), a monoclonal antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), serves as a cornerstone therapeutic option for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). However, patients with KRAS-mutant CRC present inherent resistance to CET, which directly compromises its clinical efficacy and therapeutic benefits. Zuojin Wan (ZJW), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting of Coptis chinensis Franch. and Evodia rutaecarpa (Juss.) Benth., has been documented to exert potent antitumor activity; nevertheless, its potential role in reversing CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of ZJW in overcoming CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and further characterize its key molecular targets and regulatory mechanisms. METHODS: In vitro experiments were conducted using two KRAS-mutated CRC cell lines, HCT116 and SW620. The synergistic antiproliferative effect of ZJW combined with CET was assessed via CCK-8 assay and colony formation assay. Ferroptosis induction mediated by the combination treatment was verified by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) depletion, ferrous ion (Fe2+) accumulation, and observing characteristic mitochondrial morphological alterations using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were detected to evaluate intracellular oxidative stress. Transcriptome sequencing, Western blot analysis and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were performed to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms, while plasmid transfection and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were carried out for functional validation. A nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model was established to evaluate the antitumor efficacy of the combined treatment in vivo, and immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was performed to detect the expression of relevant proteins. The primary bioactive components of ZJW were identified by mass spectrometry, and network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict the potential interactions between these active components and CRC-related signaling pathways. RESULTS: ZJW synergistically augmented the CET-mediated suppression of KRAS-mutated CRC cell proliferation and triggered significant ferroptosis, as evidenced by elevated lipid peroxidation, reduced GSH levels, increased Fe2+ accumulation, shrunken mitochondria with condensed cristae, and markedly enhanced intracellular oxidative stress. Combination treatment with ZJW and CET significantly downregulated the expression of core proteins involved in the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes, thereby disrupting intracellular redox homeostasis. Silencing of NRF2 or DHODH facilitated ferroptosis and sensitized CRC cells to CET, whereas overexpression of these two molecules abolished the synergistic antitumor effect of ZJW plus CET. In the nude mouse xenograft model, the combined regimen notably suppressed tumor growth and decreased tumor weight, and modulated the expression of ferroptosis-associated markers (NRF2, DHODH) and the lipid peroxidation indicator 4-HNE in tumor tissues. Mass spectrometry identified the major bioactive constituents of ZJW, and network pharmacology analysis predicted their potential involvement in multiple CRC-related pathways, including antioxidant defense and ferroptosis regulation. CONCLUSION: ZJW reverses CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC by inhibiting the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes to induce ferroptosis. This study provides a solid scientific basis for the clinical translation of ZJW as an adjuvant therapeutic strategy to boost the efficacy of CET in CRC treatment.

articles.title: Oudemansiella raphanipes polysaccharide alleviates DSS-induced colitis associated with gut microbiota and ZBP1-associated PANoptosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease with limited preventive options. The edible mushroom Oudemansiella raphanipes produces polysaccharides with reported bioactivity, but the effects of its purified fraction Oudemansiella raphanipes polysaccharide (UAE-ORP) on colitis remain unknown. PURPOSE AND METHODS: UAE-ORP was evaluated in mice with sodium dextran sulphate (DSS)-induced colitis using metagenomic and metabolomic analysis, as well as histological, ELISA and Western blot analysis of intestinal barrier function, ZBP1-associated PANoptosis-related proteins, and FFAR2/FFAR3 expression. RESULTS: UAE-ORP alleviated DSS-induced colonic injury, reducing the DAI scores to 1.7 ± 0.3-2.7 ± 0.5 across treatment groups and restoring colon length to 6.2 ± 0.9-8.2 ± 0.8 cm across doses. UAE-ORP was associated with attenuated ZBP1-associated PANoptosis-related protein expression, increased Lachnospiraceae abundance, and restored acetic acid and 3,4-dihydroxyphthalate levels. UAE-ORP also restored the protein expression levels of FFAR2 and FFAR3. Correlation analysis suggested a potential association between Lachnospiraceae-related metabolites and FFAR2/FFAR3 signaling. CONCLUSION: UAE-ORP alleviates DSS-induced colitis in mice. The protective effects coincide with altered gut microbiota composition, elevated microbial metabolites, restored FFAR2/FFAR3 expression, and concomitant changes in ZBP1-associated PANoptosis-related protein. These observations identify several candidate pathways warranting further investigation and provide preliminary mechanistic context for the anti-colitic activity of this mushroom polysaccharide.

articles.title: Rocbrutinib: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Rocbrutinib (; LP-168) is a fourth generation Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor with both covalent and non-covalent modes of binding, which allow it to inhibit both wildtype as well as mutant variants of BTK. It is being developed by Lupeng Pharmaceuticals primarily as a treatment for patients with B-cell malignancies. Rocbrutinib received its first approval in June 2026 in China for use in adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) that is relapsed or refractory to BTK inhibitors, and who have received ≥ 2 systemic therapies (including BTK inhibitors). This article summarizes the milestones in the development of rocbrutinib leading to its first approval in this indication.

articles.title: CYP2D6-Guided Opioid Therapy for Chronic Pain: A Multi-Center Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: The analgesic effectiveness of several opioids depends on CYP2D6-mediated metabolism to more active opioid receptor agonists. CYP2D6 activity is impacted by genetic variability and medications that inhibit CYP2D6. We conducted a pragmatic, multi-center, randomized, controlled trial to determine whether CYP2D6-guided opioid prescribing improves chronic pain. Participants were adults recruited from primary care or pain specialty clinics with at least 3 months of chronic pain treated or considered for treatment with tramadol, hydrocodone, or codeine. Participants were randomized to the usual care or CYP2D6-guided arm, in which CYP2D6 pharmacogenetic testing was performed. Healthcare professionals were recommended to avoid tramadol, hydrocodone, or codeine in patients with CYP2D6 intermediate or poor or ultra-rapid (for safety) metabolizer phenotypes based on either genotype or drug interactions. The primary outcome was the change in composite pain intensity scores from baseline to 3 months. Of 1048 enrolled participants, 282 had an actionable CYP2D6 phenotype. In this group, CYP2D6-guided recommendations did not improve the change in composite pain intensity scores from baseline to 3 months compared with usual care (mean [SD] -0.8 [2.4] vs. -0.7 [2.3]) or improve drug-gene concordance (26.8% vs. 27.1%) in the CYP2D6-guided versus usual care arm, respectively. In an exploratory analysis, participants whose therapy changed to align with their CYP2D6 phenotype had significantly improved pain scores. In conclusion, incorporating CYP2D6-guided recommendations for opioid therapy into routine practice did not change prescribing sufficiently to assess its impact on chronic pain control, suggesting that EHR-integrated CYP2D6 guidance is insufficient to change opioid prescribing for chronic pain.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics of Rifapentine and Desacetyl Rifapentine in Maternal Plasma and Breast Milk & Infant Cord Blood and Plasma: A Model-Based Analysis of Mother-Infant Pairs for Tuberculosis Prevention.
articles.abstract: IMPAACT 2001 (NCT02651259) evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of once-weekly isoniazid and rifapentine in pregnant and postpartum women for tuberculosis prevention. Rifapentine (RPT) and desacetyl rifapentine (desRPT) PK data were collected in maternal plasma, breast milk, infant cord blood, and infant plasma. Longitudinal maternal plasma and breast milk RPT and desRPT concentrations were characterized using a multicompartment PK model with biophase effect compartments (NONMEM v7.4). Rate parameters describing drug entry into breast milk from plasma and breast milk-to-plasma ratio parameters were estimated. For mother-infant pairs, maternal plasma PK was simulated for the last RPT dose pre-delivery (with HIV and partum status covariates), and concentration ratios (observed infant cord blood or plasma relative to simulated maternal plasma) were calculated at the infant PK sample collection time. For RPT and desRPT, derived equilibration half-lives were 0.568 hr and 0.439 hr, and estimated concentration ratios of breast milk to maternal plasma were 0.0236 and 0.0411, respectively, indicating rapid equilibration between maternal plasma and breast milk and a minimal extent of drug excretion into breast milk. Maximum relative infant dose was estimated at <1%. Within 72 hours of maternal dosing, median concentration ratios of observed infant cord blood and plasma to predicted maternal plasma were approximately 0.280 and 0.612 for RPT and 0.493 and 1.83 for desRPT, respectively. RPT crosses the placenta and is measurable in infant plasma at concentrations unlikely to be clinically significant. Breast milk concentrations are very low, supporting safe use of RPT in breastfeeding women.

articles.title: Antispasmodic and analgesic strategies for renal colic in pregnancy: a comprehensive analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Analgesia remains the paramount priority in the clinical management of gestational renal colic, yet established protocols are frequently constrained by contraindications. While antispasmodic intervention emerges as a viable alternative, the definitive pharmacological choice remains elusive. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness and safety of commonly used antispasmodic and analgesic strategies for pregnancy-related renal colic using network and pairwise meta-analyses. METHOD: A literature review was undertaken utilizing three English-language databases and four Chinese-language databases, encompassing publications up to 1 January 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that satisfied the inclusion criteria were selected for analysis. The Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool was employed to evaluate the risk of bias. Statistical analyses were performed, encompassing intervention comparison and ranking, assessment of consistency and heterogeneity, evaluation of publication bias, as well as meta-regression, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: The study included ten RCTs with 936 patients. Four dimensions for the RCTs had a low risk of bias, with one dimension having "some concerns." In network meta-analyses, phloroglucinol was most effective in relieving pain within 1 h, followed by progesterone, while anisodamine was least effective. Phloroglucinol caused the least side effects like nausea and dizziness compared to progesterone and anisodamine. In pairwise meta-analyses, phloroglucinol had a lower 6-h pain recurrence rate and fewer side effects like blurred vision and palpitations than anisodamine. Variations in phloroglucinol dosage contributed to heterogeneity, but subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed result stability. CONCLUSION: Phloroglucinol is the preferred treatment for renal colic pain during pregnancy due to its efficacy and safety. It can be combined with progesterone, but anisodamine is not advised. Further high-quality research is necessary to confirm this finding. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42022377502.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of first- versus second-generation fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) inhibitors in advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with FGFR alterations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We reviewed the clinical studies on fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) inhibitors for the treatment of urothelial carcinoma to conduct the meta-analysis of clinical efficacy and safety, aiming to provide more precise treatment options for patients with FGFR alterations. METHOD: We performed the literature search and screening, then calculated and analyzed using the STATA 14.0 software and Review Manager 5.3 software. RESULTS: A total of 1528 patients from seventeen studies focusing on seven different FGFR inhibitors were collected. The efficacy analysis indicated the pooled objective response rate (ORR) was 32% (95% CI 26% to 39%) and the pooled disease control rate (DCR) was 64% (95% CI 53% to 75%) for patients with FGFR alterations treated with FGFR inhibitors. The pooled ORR and DCR of second-generation FGFR inhibitors were both significantly higher than those of first-generation FGFR inhibitors (ORR: 0.35, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.41 versus 0.07, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.16, p < 0.001; DCR: 0.68, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.75 versus 0.27, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.40, p < 0.001). The safety analysis indicated any-grade TRAEs were comparable between first- and second-generation FGFR inhibitors, but grade ≥3 TRAEs were significantly less frequent with second-generation FGFR inhibitors versus first-generation FGFR inhibitors (0.49, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.57 versus 0.67, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.76; p = 0.006). The common target toxicities associated with FGFR inhibitors, such as hyperphosphatemia, stomatitis and PPES, were more frequently occurred in second-generation FGFR inhibitors compared to first-generation FGFR inhibitors. CONCLUSION: The second-generation FGFR inhibitors have advantages in both efficacy and safety, but special adverse reactions still require additional attention.

articles.title: A meta-analysis of berberine combined with brain-gut axis-targeted agents for diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prevalence of diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is high and significantly impairs patient quality of life. Berberine, a naturally occurring isoquinoline alkaloid, shows promise in combination with brain-gut axis-targeted drugs for relieving abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhoea in IBS-D. However, current clinical evidence remains insufficient to conclusively substantiate its efficacy. AIM OF THE STUDY: Through a systematic literature review and meta-analysis, this work comprehensively evaluated the efficacy and safety of berberine in combination with brain-gut axis-targeted medications for the treatment of IBS-D, thereby providing evidence to inform clinical practice. MATERIALS AND METHODS: On 1 December 2025, a comprehensive search was conducted across ten databases, including PubMed, Web of Science (WOS), the Cochrane Library, and Embase, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating berberine in combination with brain-gut axis-targeted medications. Two reviewers independently screened the literature according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, followed by data extraction. The risk of bias tool developed by the Cochrane Collaboration was used to assess the methodological quality of the included studies, and data were analyzed using RStudio software. When two or more studies had comparable interventions and outcome measures, a meta-analysis was conducted, otherwise, a qualitative synthesis was performed. The certainty of evidence for each outcome was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: A total of 19 RCTs involving 1,489 participants were included in the analysis. Compared with the control groups, the intervention groups showed significant improvements in IBS-D symptoms and patient quality of life. Specifically, combination therapy incorporating berberine significantly increased the overall treatment response rate (odds ratio = 4.19, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 3.13-5.61). With respect to continuous outcomes, combination therapy significantly reduced overall symptom scores (standardized mean difference (SMD) = -3.47, 95% CI: -6.65 to -0.29), particularly reflected by reductions in abdominal pain and bloating severity, along with improvements in diarrhoea-related symptoms. Furthermore, no serious adverse events were reported across the included trials. CONCLUSION: Berberine combined with brain-gut axis-targeted medications shows promising efficacy and acceptable safety in the treatment of IBS-D. However, existing studies are limited by small sample sizes and methodological weaknesses, and the overall strength of evidence remains insufficient. Larger, rigorously designed RCTs are needed to further confirm its efficacy and safety. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251238184, identifier CRD420251238184.

articles.title: Research trends of nanotechnology in coronary heart disease: a bibliometric analysis from 2012 to 2025.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with conventional therapeutic strategies limited by non-specific targeting, low bioavailability, and systemic off-target effects. Nanomaterials, leveraging their unique physicochemical properties, have shown immense potential in CHD diagnosis and therapy. However, the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and thematic evolution of nanomaterials in CHD have not been systematically evaluated. METHODS: Relevant publications from 2012 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases. Bibliometric and visualization analyses were performed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Scimago Graphica. The study evaluated publication trends, international and institutional collaboration networks, co-occurrence patterns, citation characteristics, and emerging research themes through keyword clustering and burst detection. RESULTS: A total of 2,709 publications were included, demonstrating a continuous increase in research activity during the study period. China and the United States were the leading contributors in publication output and international collaboration. Major institutional contributors included Harvard University, Massachusetts General Hospital, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses identified several major research directions, including nanobiosensing, molecular imaging, targeted nanoparticle delivery, and regenerative medicine. Among these evolving themes, immune-inflammatory mechanisms, macrophage/monocyte regulation, oxidative stress, and microenvironmental modulation have emerged as increasingly prominent research directions in nanotechnology-based CHD investigation. CONCLUSION: This bibliometric analysis provides an overview of the global development and knowledge evolution of nanotechnology research in CHD from 2012 to 2025. The findings indicate that immune-inflammatory mechanisms represent an emerging research theme within the broader landscape of cardiovascular nanotechnology. The growing attention toward immune modulation and disease-specific microenvironment regulation identified in this study may represent important directions for future translational research in cardiovascular nanotechnology.

articles.title: Efficacy and neuroprotective effects of tetramethylpyrazine in animal models of spinal cord injury: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and exploratory machine-learning study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a severe neurological disorder characterized by persistent motor dysfunction and complex secondary injury processes. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) has shown potential neuroprotective effects in experimental SCI; however, the overall efficacy and factors associated with its therapeutic effects remain unclear. This study systematically evaluated the efficacy of TMP in animal models of SCI and explored potential efficacy-related experimental factors using machine-learning methods. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang and VIP databases were searched for controlled animal studies investigating TMP treatment in SCI. Hedges' g and corresponding 95% confidence intervals were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses and assessments of small-study effects were performed where sufficient data were available. An exploratory XGBoost model combined with SHAP analysis was used to evaluate study-level characteristics potentially associated with BBB effect sizes. Model performance was assessed using repeated 10-fold cross-validation with 20 repetitions, and feature-importance stability was evaluated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. RESULTS: Forty-two animal studies were included. Compared with control treatment, TMP significantly improved locomotor recovery, with progressively greater improvements in BBB scores from day 1 to day 28 after injury. TMP also improved inclined-plane performance at most evaluated time points. Biochemical analyses indicated that TMP alleviated oxidative stress by reducing malondialdehyde levels and increasing superoxide dismutase activity. TMP treatment was also associated with reduced concentrations of several pro-inflammatory cytokines and improvements in apoptosis-related outcomes. Repeated 10-fold cross-validation showed poor predictive performance (median R2 = -0.314). Bootstrap analyses relatively consistently ranked injury level and sex among the most important features; however, these findings were interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than as validated predictors. CONCLUSION: The available preclinical evidence indicates that TMP promotes locomotor recovery and exerts antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic effects in animal models of SCI. The exploratory machine-learning analysis did not demonstrate reliable predictive performance, and the observed feature-importance patterns should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Further standardized animal experiments and well-designed translational studies are required. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261459838, identifier CRD420261459838.

articles.title: Reprocessing Mass Spectra from Therapeutic Drug Monitoring to Unveil Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and Quantify Phenoconversion of Escitalopram Metabolism in CYP2C19-Genotyped Patients.
articles.abstract: Escitalopram is a frequently prescribed antidepressant drug. CYP2C19 genotype is a major determinant of escitalopram metabolism and treatment outcome. However, real-life studies show a high degree of genotype-phenotype mismatch in escitalopram metabolism. The present study aimed to identify comedication with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and quantify phenoconversion of escitalopram metabolism in CYP2C19-genotyped patients by reprocessing high-resolution mass spectra from therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) analyses. Patients were included from a combined TDM/pharmacogenetics (PGx) laboratory facility in Oslo, Norway. TDM profiles of escitalopram and CYP2C19 genotypes were available in the laboratory database. Reprocessing of high-resolution mass spectra by exact mass and fragment detection identified possible comedication with pantoprazole, esomeprazole/omeprazole or lansoprazole using mzCloud reference library. Patients were grouped as normal metabolizers (NMs), intermediate metabolizers (IMs), poor metabolizers (PMs), rapid metabolizers (RM), or ultrarapid metabolizers (UM). Primary outcome measure was N-desmethylescitalopram-to-escitalopram metabolic ratio (MR; CYP2C19 biomarker) in UMs vs. PMs. 2818 patients were included, constituting 2373 without and 445 (15.8%) with PPIs. Most patients were females (64.2%). Regarding CYP2C19 phenotype distribution, the cohort comprised 39.3% NMs, 29.3% IMs, 2.6% PMs, 24.6% RMs, and 4.2% UMs. Escitalopram MR was 4.5-fold higher in CYP2C19 UMs vs. PMs without PPIs (P < 0.001), while this difference was 2.8-fold in pantoprazole users (P < 0.001), and 1.8-fold in esomeprazole/omeprazole users (P = 0.2). In conclusion, PPIs show significant phenoconversion of CYP2C19-mediated escitalopram metabolism with esomeprazole/omeprazole exhibiting a stronger effect than pantoprazole. The novel method for identification of interacting comedications in TDM samples illustrates the innovative potential of high-resolution mass spectrometry in precision medicine.

articles.title: Evidence on Glutathione and Boosters for Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) adversely affects treatment efficacy and quality of life. Despite studies on glutathione (GSH) or GSH boosters' antioxidative effects for prevention, optimal management remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to consolidate and critically appraise the current evidence and to compare the efficacy of GSH and GSH boosters for the prevention of CIPN. The MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL databases were searched through March 2025. Twenty-five RCTs involving 1625 patients were included. No intervention significantly reduced all-grade CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine (odds ratio [OR] 0.19, 95% credible intervals [CrI] 0.05-0.63), GSH (OR 0.34, 95% CrI 0.13-0.79) and vitamin E (OR 0.33, 95% CrI 0.11-0.91) were associated with a reduced incidence of grade 3/4 CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine ranked highest for both all-grade and grade 3/4 CIPN prevention. These findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with pre-existing neuropathy but were not retained in analyses restricted to double-blind studies. Overall, N-acetylcysteine, GSH, and vitamin E were associated with potential reductions in severe CIPN, with N-acetylcysteine consistently ranking highest, although these associations should be regarded as preliminary. Further rigorously conducted and adequately powered trials are warranted to confirm these findings and evaluate agents demonstrating potential benefits.

articles.title: Metformin Lowers Fasting Hyperglycemia by Increasing Glucose Clearance in People with Moderately Controlled Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Metformin is the most frequently prescribed antidiabetic drug worldwide; however, the mechanism by which it lowers blood glucose remains incompletely understood. The objective of this study was to examine the effects of metformin on whole-body and specifically on hepatic glucose and energy metabolism in type 2 diabetes. METHODS: This open repeated-measures pilot study examined this question using Positional Isotopomer NMR Tracer Analysis (PINTA) to assess rates of endogenous glucose production (VEGP), hepatic pyruvate carboxylase flux (VPC), and citrate synthase (VCS) flux in 16 men with moderately controlled type 2 diabetes (T2D; BMI 30 ± 3 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.4 ± 1.4%) undergoing two examination days with (M+; 1 g twice daily) and without metformin (M-) treatment. Hepatic ATP and glycogen concentrations were quantified by 31P/13C magnetic resonance spectroscopy. RESULTS: M+ reduced fasting glycemia by 18%, which could mostly be attributed to a 24% increase in rates of whole-body glucose clearance. Surprisingly, these changes were accompanied by a 58% increase in VPC and a 34% increase in VCS, due to a 26% increase in plasma glucagon concentrations. The increase in VPC was offset by reductions in the contributions of glycerol conversion to glucose resulting in no change in VEGP. Metformin decreased hepatic ATP content by 16% and increased plasma GDF-15 concentrations, but did not alter rates of net hepatic glycogenolysis. CONCLUSION: Metformin treatment in male individuals of European ancestry with moderately controlled T2D decreases blood glucose concentrations by increasing rates of whole-body glucose clearance. Metformin further inhibits glycerol-derived gluconeogenesis, which is consistent with complex IV, not complex I, being the molecular target of metformin action. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/ ): NCT04088851.

articles.title: Ciprocopan: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Ciprocopan (®) is a small molecule inhibitor of complement factor B, which is a key component of the alternative complement pathway. It is being developed by Haisco Pharmaceutical Group for the treatment of complement-mediated disorders. In July 2026, ciprocopan received its first approval for treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria (PNH) who have not previously received treatment with a complement inhibitor therapy in China. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of ciprocopan leading to this first approval.

articles.title: Four-week supplementation with a blackcurrant formulation enhances cognitive performance, reduces mental fatigue and modulates peripheral monoamine metabolism in older adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Age-related cognitive decline is an increasing concern in older adults. While blackcurrants (Ribes nigrum) have shown promise in improving cognitive outcomes in younger adults, their efficacy in supporting cognitive function in older adults is largely unexplored. METHODS: In this randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded crossover study of healthy older adults (62 ± 1 years), 26 of the 30 participants enrolled completed the study per protocol. Participants consumed either a placebo or a flavonoid-rich blackcurrant formula (BCF, 7.8 mg anthocyanins/kg body weight freeze-dried blackcurrant, 200 mg L-theanine, and 100 mg pine bark extract) in a beverage format daily for 4 weeks, with interventions separated by a two-week washout period. For each intervention, cognitive and mood outcomes were assessed following a single dose (acute) and after 4 weeks' supplementation. Platelet MAO-B activity, circulating neurotransmitter concentrations, and anthocyanin, L-theanine and sarmentosin bioavailability were measured from venous blood samples drawn at baseline, 1 h, 2.4 h and 4 wk after intervention supplementation. RESULTS: A significant reduction in Rapid Visual Information Processing (RVIP) false alarms (p = 0.022) and a strong trend in reduced mental fatigue (p = 0.046, q = 0.067) were measured following 4 weeks of BCF supplementation. Reduction in biomarkers of MAO activity were measured following acute supplementation with BCF, but not placebo, with significant treatment × time interactions (q < 0.01) for platelet MAO-B activity, plasma 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid and 3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine concentrations. These changes corresponded with significant reductions (q < 0.05) in circulating neurotransmitter metabolites xanthurenic acid, 3-methoxy-4-hydroxyphenylglycol and vanillylmandelic acid. CONCLUSION: Findings from this study indicate that 4 weeks of BCF supplementation sustained attention in healthy older adults, extending evidence for BCF-related cognitive benefits across both younger and older populations. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://anzctr.org.au/, identifier: ACTRN12621001590853.

articles.title: Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies.
articles.abstract: Efficient delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) into the nucleus remains a major bottleneck in nonviral gene therapy, particularly in post-mitotic and slowly dividing cells where the nuclear envelope constitutes a permanent barrier to passive entry. This review considers the two main strategies for active nuclear targeting: nuclear localisation signal (NLS) peptides, which recruit importin-α/β receptors directly to DNA cargo, and DNA nuclear targeting sequences (DTS), which exploit NLS-bearing transcription factors to mediate piggyback nuclear import. Rather than re-cataloguing nuclear import biology, we focus on the conditions under which each strategy succeeds or fails, incorporating advances in nuclear pore complex architecture and permeability, karyopherin-FG-nucleoporin electrostatics, and cytoplasmic constraints such as barrier-to-autointegration factor (BAF)-mediated clustering of exogenous DNA. NLS classes are compared with universal (SV40 enhancer), inducible (NF-κB) and tissue-specific (SMGA, SP-C, T1α) DTS elements, and four chemical coupling strategies are evaluated across peptide-, polymer- and lipid-based nanoassemblies. To address the near-absence of NLS/DTS mechanisms in current clinical pDNA programmes, we propose the Nuclear Accessibility Index (NAI): a three-axis framework integrating cell division status, carrier-DNA accessibility and intracellular signalling context. Treating the NAI as an axis vector rather than a summed score defines permissive, conditional and excluded regions of the design space. Two matter in practice: one in which highly proliferative cells render active targeting redundant, and one in which the rate-limiting problem is carrier engineering rather than the addition of a signal. The NAI offers design principles for nuclear-targeted nanocarriers and defines the preconditions for therapeutically relevant active import.

articles.title: Mushroom derived extracellular vesicles: biogenesis, molecular cargo, therapeutic potential, and translational value.
articles.abstract: Mushroom-derived extracellular vesicles (MDEVs) are categorized as a novel natural nanotherapeutic, showing significant anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-aging effects making them suitable for biomedical and aesthetic fields. This review comprehensively summarizes the current knowledge on MDEVs with special focus on their biogenesis, molecular composition, purification, characterization, mechanisms of ingestion and function. Main focus includes the comparative characterization processes, methods for improving the stability of MDEVs, current trends in scalable isolation techniques, bioengineering approaches for targeted delivery, and multi-omics characterization. From the published literature it is evident that most of the edible mushrooms release EVs loaded with phenolics, polysaccharides, lipids, enzymes, and RNAs showing antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and skin-rejuvenating activities. Additionally, MDEVs inhibit NF-κB/MAPK signaling and proinflammatory cytokines, which reduce neuroinflammation and improve cognition in vivo. They also influence collagen remodeling, fibroblast activity, and melanogenesis in skin health, indicating their potential for anti-aging and wound repair applications. This review discusses the challenges in standardization, safety profiling, multimodal bioactivity and highlights benefits in biocompatibility. By providing the mechanistic insights, therapeutic potential, and translational strategies, this review highlights MDEVs as next-generation natural nanotherapeutics and provide the future directions for clinical and cosmeceutical translation.

articles.title: Antibody-drug conjugates as promising platform for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: molecular insights, drug-delivery challenges, and emerging therapeutic targets.
articles.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is the second most prevalent primary hepatic malignancy with increasing incidence, poor prognosis, recurrence, and limited therapies. Currently, surgical resection remains the only potentially curative treatment for iCCA. The main challenge, even after surgery, is that small or poorly cellular liver tumors may recur a year later if minimal residual disease goes undetected. Additionally, the majority of chemotherapy and targeted therapies have modest clinical benefit due to tumor heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have recently emerged as a promising targeted therapeutic platform by combining the tumor specificity of monoclonal antibodies with highly potent cytotoxic payloads, thereby enabling selective drug delivery while minimizing systemic toxicity. This review comprehensively summarizes the molecular landscape of iCCA relevant to ADC development and discusses clinically significant targets, including HER2, FGFR2, TROP2, Claudin-1, MUC1, EpCAM, and EGFR. The structural and functional significance of ADC components, including antibodies, linkers, and payloads, are also discussed in relation to therapeutic efficacy and safety. Furthermore, current preclinical and clinical progress involving ADC-based therapies for iCCA and related cholangiocarcinoma is highlighted. Tumor heterogenicity, drug resistance, desmoplastic tumor microenvironment, and low antigen binding are among the primary barriers to the development of ADCs for iCCA that are critically discussed. Additionally, the prospects for the next generation, including bispecific ADCs and dual-payload conjugates for iCCA, were explored. Collectively, ADCs represent a rapidly evolving precision oncology platform with considerable potential to improve therapeutic outcomes and future management strategies for patients with iCCA.

articles.title: Calcium-Sensing Receptor-NLRP3 Inflammasome Signaling in Cardiovascular Diseases: Preclinical Evidence and Translational Perspectives.
articles.abstract: The chronic low-grade inflammation driven by NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is increasingly acknowledged as an underlying mechanism of myocardial infarction, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and atherosclerosis. Extracellular Ca2+, amino acids, and other ligands link to intracellular Ca2+ overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, reactive oxygen species generation, thioredoxin-interacting protein activation, and NF-κB-dependent inflammasome priming via the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). Experimental studies indicate that CaSR may activate the NLRP3 inflammasome through these pathways in a cell- and context-dependent manner. In preclinical cardiovascular models, CaSR-mediated NLRP3 signaling has been implicated in neutrophil- and macrophage-mediated post-MI remodeling, atrial cardiomyocyte inflammatory remodeling in atrial fibrillation, and vascular smooth muscle and endothelial dysfunction in hypertension and atherosclerosis. Importantly, CaSR signalling may exert pro-inflammatory or protective effects depending on the cell type, ligand, dose, disease stage, and local microenvironment. Here, we review preclinical evidence and emerging translational evidence separately, highlighting the CaSR-NLRP3 signalling in cardiovascular disease, describe pharmacologic approaches that may modulate CaSR, NLRP3, or downstream inflammatory pathways, and identify key mechanistic and clinical knowledge gaps. Although direct clinical evidence for a complete CaSR-NLRP3 axis in cardiovascular diseases remains limited, these findings support further investigation of context-specific CaSR-NLRP3 crosstalk as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: From stress cytokine to drug target: The translational landscape of growth differentiation factor 15.
articles.abstract: Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) is a stress-responsive cytokine that translates cellular injury, metabolic imbalance, and disease burden into systemic physiological responses. Discovery of its hindbrain-restricted receptor, glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor family receptor α-like (GFRAL) and cosignaling partner rearranged during transfection (RET), established a dedicated neuroendocrine axis (GDF15-GFRAL-RET) linking stress to appetite suppression, nausea, and autonomic effects on energy expenditure. Initially regarded as a passive disease biomarker, GDF15 is now recognized as an active mediator in cancer-related anorexia-cachexia syndrome, chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, obesity, aging, cardiovascular disease, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal diseases, neurodegeneration, eating disorders, and hyperemesis gravidarum. This expanding biology has driven parallel development of GFRAL agonists and antagonists, as well as approaches to bind and eliminate circulating GDF15 in the treatment of illness behaviors associated with these numerous disease states. Here we review GDF15 biology and signaling from a medicinal chemistry perspective, examining reported structure-activity relationship-guided drug discovery across biologics and small molecules, including patents and ongoing clinical trials targeting the GDF15-GFRAL-RET axis. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) is a stress-induced cytokine that signals through the hindbrain-restricted GFRAL-RET receptor complex to regulate appetite, nausea, and energy balance. This review highlights advances in understanding GDF15 biology, its role in disease, and synthesizes medicinal chemistry efforts targeting this pathway. By integrating structure-activity relationships, biologics, and small molecule approaches, this study outlines therapeutic strategies and translational challenges in modulating the GDF15-GFRAL-RET axis.

articles.title: Clinical Pharmacokinetics of Polmacoxib (CG100649): A Tissue-Selective Dual COX-2 and Carbonic Anhydrase I/II Inhibitor.
articles.abstract: Polmacoxib (CG100649; Acelex) is a first-in-class non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug that combines selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibition with high-affinity binding to carbonic anhydrase I/II (CA-I/II). Approved for osteoarthritis in South Korea (2015) and India (2023), it exhibits pharmacokinetic (PK) properties distinct from other coxibs. The objective of this review is to review the clinical PK and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) profile of polmacoxib, compare it with other coxibs, and identify key evidence gaps. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through June 2026, supplemented by reference lists and regulatory, patent, and Protein Data Bank records. The clinical PK profile of polmacoxib is dominated by erythrocyte sequestration via high-affinity binding to CA-I/II. After oral dosing, whole-blood concentrations exceed plasma concentrations by approximately 50-78 on average, with individual values approaching 120-fold, and terminal half-lives are approximately 121-203 h in blood and 100-167 h in plasma. A 2-compartment whole-blood model with mixed zero- and first-order absorption best describes the data, with serum iron, white-cell count, and age identified as covariates of clearance. The 2-mg once-daily dose substantially inhibits thromboxane B2 and ex vivo PGE2, with only modest, dose-dependent inhibition of urinary prostacyclin metabolite (PGI-M) that is of comparable magnitude, although less sustained, to celecoxib 200 mg after single dosing; the 2-mg dose is noninferior to celecoxib 200 mg on WOMAC pain endpoints in osteoarthritis. Ketoconazole produces only modest changes in plasma exposure, and PK data in hepatic impairment, renal impairment, older people, and non-Korean populations remain limited. Polmacoxib has a unique PK profile among coxibs, driven by erythrocyte carbonic anhydrase binding, which supports its proposed tissue-selective pharmacology. Further studies in special populations, drug-drug interactions, and post-marketing settings are needed to support broader global use.

articles.title: Research progress on Bergenia purpurascens: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Bergenia purpurascens (Hook.f.et Thoms.) Engl., a perennial herb belonging to the genus Bergenia (family Saxifragaceae), is primarily distributed in southwestern China and mountainous regions of Nepal, Bhutan, and northeastern India, where it has a long history of medicinal use. A systematic retrieval of relevant literature was conducted on PubMed, Scopus, CNKI, and Web of Science using "Bergenia purpurascens" and "Bergenia" as primary keywords, supplemented by "chemical metabolite," "pharmacological action," and "resource distribution" as search terms. This review systematically summarizes the research progress on the botanical characteristics, resource distribution, medicinal parts, chemical metabolites, pharmacological activity, toxicology, and modern applications of B. purpurascens. Its primary active metabolites include phenolics, including bergenin, gallic acid, and arbutin, which exhibit expectorant, antitussive, anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, antitumor, and neuroprotective activities. Recent studies elucidating the bergenin biosynthetic pathway provide a basis for industrial production. Additionally, B. purpurascens shows broad development potential in pharmaceuticals, health products, cosmetics, and landscaping. This review provides a scientific basis for further research and comprehensive utilization of B. purpurascens.

articles.title: Chemically modified gelatin derivatives: synthetic strategies, physicochemical properties, biodegradation, drug delivery and biomedical applications.
articles.abstract: Gelatin, the hydrolysate of collagen, has been used as a food ingredient as well as a pharmaceutical excipient since ancient times. Of late, it has attracted renewed interest as a constituent of drug delivery systems (DDS) because of its amicability to easily transform into various structural forms such as hydrogel, nanoparticles, and microsphere among others. Further, to meet the requirements for the fabrication of DDS, researchers have attempted various kinds of chemical modifications of the native gelatin. Some of the major chemical modification strategies of gelatin include amination, thiolation, PEGylation, acrylation and selenation, among others. Increasing evidences so far have established that chemically modified derivatives of gelatin exhibit superior physicochemical properties compared to native gelatin to support drug delivery applications such as higher drug loading efficiency and improved drug release kinetics, biocompatibility, biodegradability and pharmacokinetic profile. Accordingly, chemically modified derivatives of gelatin have been preferred over native gelatin for biomedical applications. Moreover, the growing popularity of chemically modified derivatives of gelatin has prompted their commercial production. In view of these considerations, a dedicated review article summarizing the biochemistry of gelatin, various synthetic strategies used for the preparation of chemically modified derivatives of gelatin, mechanistic discussion on the superiority of the Physicochemical properties of gelatin derivatives along with recent progress and concerns linked to their biomedical applications, is warranted. The present review article addresses this objective by providing a comprehensive, critical, and up-to-date summary of chemically modified derivatives of gelatin.

articles.title: Teaching the true cost of medicines: white paper for a green and sustainable pharmacology curriculum.
articles.abstract: The drug lifecycle imposes a growing environmental burden, evident in pharmaceutical pollution, escalating consumption of finite resources (energy, water, and raw materials) and a substantial carbon footprint. Meeting these challenges requires more than technological fixes; it demands a workforce trained to recognise, evaluate, and reduce the environmental impacts of medicines while safeguarding patient outcomes. However, recent scoping and systematic reviews consistently note a gap in health professions education: few curricula provide structured, evidence-informed approaches for integrating environmental sustainability and planetary health into pharmacology and related training. The discipline of pharmacology is uniquely suited for integrating green and sustainability principles because it sits at the decision-point where molecular mechanisms become real-world medicine use and environmental impact. This paper presents a white paper proposing a Green and Sustainable Pharmacology Curriculum and an actionable strategy for embedding sustainability principles within core pharmacology teaching. Targeted at biomedical scientists, pharmacists, and prescribers, the curriculum is designed to strengthen decision-making across the medicine lifecycle, including greener selection, rational use, and responsible disposal. We outline a curriculum development framework that applies Understanding by Design and outcome-based evaluation through four streamlined steps: (1) needs analysis, (2) curation of priority content topics, (3) constructive alignment of learning activities with intended competencies, and (4) assessment aligned to learning outcomes. By offering an adaptable blueprint for local implementation, this white paper aims to accelerate adoption by pharmacology departments worldwide. Ultimately, the curriculum seeks to shift learners from concerned global citizens to empowered pharmacologists with personal agency implement workplace changes that mitigate environmental harms and to serve as thought leaders advancing sustainable healthcare.

articles.title: Monoclonal antibodies associated IgA nephropathy or other nephropathies.
articles.abstract: The use of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) has revolutionized the treatment of autoimmune, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. However, accumulating evidence indicates that biologic therapies may be associated with renal adverse events, including various types of glomerulonephritis. The aim of this review was to summarize all reports available in the scientific literature regarding the occurrence of IgA nephropathy after monoclonal antibody treatment. Additionally, the risk of other glomerulonephritis after biologic therapy was discussed. IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most commonly reported glomerular lesion associated with monoclonal antibody therapy, particularly with TNF-α inhibitors such as infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab, and etanercept, as well as with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1 (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) and interleukin (ustekinumab) pathways. Proposed mechanisms include immune dysregulation with a shift toward Th2 and Th17-dependent responses, increased production of galactose-deficient IgA1, complement activation, formation of circulating immune complexes, and loss of immune tolerance. In some cases, drug discontinuation and glucocorticoid therapy have resulted in partial or complete disease remission, although progression to end-stage renal disease has also been reported. Due to the potential severity of these complications, initial and periodic monitoring of renal function and urinalysis are recommended in patients receiving monoclonal antibody therapy. Early recognition of renal involvement and prompt treatment modification can improve prognosis.

articles.title: Personalized anticoagulant therapy in venous thromboembolism: current role of direct oral anticoagulants, unmet clinical needs, and future perspectives on Factor XI inhibition.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The introduction of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has transformed the management of VTE by providing effective and convenient alternatives to vitamin K antagonists. However, despite their favorable efficacy-safety profile, clinically relevant bleeding, treatment individualization, and the management of patients with competing thrombotic and hemorrhagic risks remain important unmet clinical needs. Contemporary VTE management increasingly requires a personalized approach integrating clinical characteristics, comorbidities, biomarkers, and real-world evidence to optimize anticoagulant selection, treatment intensity, and duration. Large prospective registries have expanded our understanding of VTE across heterogeneous clinical settings, including cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative VTE, incidental and subsegmental pulmonary embolism, and other high-risk populations frequently underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. In parallel, emerging prognostic tools, including D-dimer, hemoglobin, inflammatory indices, lipid-related biomarkers, and machine-learning-based prediction models, are contributing to a more refined assessment of thrombotic and bleeding risk. These emerging therapies are being evaluated as potential strategies to reduce bleeding while maintaining antithrombotic efficacy; however, recent phase III findings have demonstrated heterogeneous efficacy across clinical indications, emphasizing that their future role is likely to be indication-specific. This narrative review examines the current role of DOACs in VTE management, discusses the clinical and biological determinants of individualized anticoagulant therapy, and critically appraises the evolving and heterogeneous evidence for Factor XI inhibition as a potential future anticoagulant strategy.

articles.title: MitoQ in sepsis-associated acute lung injury: redox pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SALI) is characterised by mitochondrial oxidative stress, bioenergetic dysfunction, dysregulated inflammation, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier. MitoQ is a mitochondria-targeted redox modulator with experimental evidence of mitochondrial and pulmonary protection, making it a candidate strategy for limiting oxidative injury in SALI. This critical narrative review evaluates the redox pharmacology of MitoQ, direct pulmonary and sepsis-related evidence, mechanistic links between mitochondrial damage and innate immune signalling, and the major requirements for clinical translation. Available studies show that MitoQ reduces mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation, preserves membrane potential and ATP production, and attenuates epithelial, endothelial, and alveolar-capillary barrier injury. Mechanistic studies further support links among mitochondrial dysfunction, abnormal mitochondrial DNA exposure, cGAS-STING signalling, NLRP3-GSDMD activation, pyroptosis, and pulmonary barrier failure. However, these downstream pathways have not yet been causally linked to MitoQ treatment in infection-associated SALI, and pulmonary or intramitochondrial drug exposure remains poorly defined. Human studies demonstrate oral feasibility and systemic redox pharmacodynamic activity but have not established pulmonary target engagement or clinical efficacy. Current evidence therefore supports MitoQ primarily as an upstream mitochondrial redox modulator with potential to preserve alveolar-capillary function. Future studies should prioritise post-onset treatment, pulmonary and mitochondrial target engagement, pathway-specific causal validation, and assessment of host defence to determine its translational potential in SALI.

articles.title: Nanocarriers in psychiatry: a comprehensive review of emerging frontiers in the management of psychiatric disorders.
articles.abstract: Psychiatric disorders are characterized by clinically significant disturbances in cognition, emotional regulation, and behavior and represent a substantial global health burden. Pharmacological management relies primarily on antidepressants, anxiolytics, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, hypnotics, and stimulants. However, conventional therapy may be limited by unfavorable physicochemical properties, variable pharmacokinetics, suboptimal brain exposure, frequent dosing, and systemic adverse effects, which may compromise therapeutic outcomes and long-term treatment adherence. Nanocarrier-based drug delivery systems have emerged as a promising approach to address some of these limitations. By optimizing particle size, composition, morphology, and surface characteristics, nanocarriers may improve drug solubility and stability, modify pharmacokinetic and release profiles, protect therapeutic agents from degradation, and facilitate brain delivery through the blood-brain barrier-associated transport mechanisms or nose-to-brain pathways. Controlled or sustained release may additionally reduce dosing frequency and improve patients' compliance. This review critically examines organic, inorganic, and hybrid nanocarrier systems investigated for psychotropic drug delivery, with particular emphasis on brain delivery mechanisms, safety considerations, clinical translation, regulatory challenges, and emerging strategies for psychiatric nanomedicine.

articles.title: Microencapsulation of an amphotericin B-solubilising mucolytic deep eutectic solvent for enhanced oral delivery to treat cystic fibrosis.
