articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop an innovative oral formulation of Amphotericin B (AmB) for the treatment of intestinal symptoms related to cystic fibrosis (CF) using microcapsules produced via the prilling/vibration technique. The use of a mucolytic Deep Eutectic Solvent (DESolve) aimed to improve the solubility of AmB and its diffusion through the mucus barrier by reducing its viscosity. Diffusion tests in purified intestinal mucus and mucin confirmed the ability to penetrate the thick mucus barrier typical of CF, enhancing drug availability at the target site. In vitro distribution studies on Caco-2/HT29 MTX E-12 cells showed that DESolve markedly increased the amount of cell-associated AmB compared with H2OAmB, indicating greater drug association with the epithelial compartment, which may facilitate AmB access to the cell membrane, where it could potentially exert its ion-channel-forming activity. To enable oral administration and protect the drug from gastric degradation, AmB solubilised in DESolve (DESAmB) was microencapsulated as a core using the prilling/vibration technique. An outer polymer shell that protects AmB from gastric degradation and ensures targeted release in the small intestine was chosen. The microcapsules were successfully produced, achieving a high yield (90.49%) and encapsulation efficiency (96.04%). Dimensional analysis and scanning electron microscopy confirmed a uniform size distribution, spherical shape, smooth surface, free of cracks and pores. Swelling studies and drug release tests in simulated gastrointestinal fluid demonstrated the formulation's ability to release AmB in the intestinal environment. These results highlight the potential of the dual strategy, i.e. the use of a mucolytic DESolve and microcapsules with targeted release in the intestine, as an innovative, stable and effective strategy for the oral administration of AmB, offering a more accessible alternative for CF patients and improving treatment adherence.

articles.title: Evaluating the effect of griseofulvin on the disintegration properties of tablets.
articles.abstract: Understanding how active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) influence tablet disintegration remains essential for optimising oral drug product performance. In this work, we present an integrated, data-driven framework that combines deep-learning-based image segmentation, automated regime detection and mechanistic modelling to characterise liquid absorption and swelling behaviours from sessile drop experiments. Using this workflow, we investigated the effect of incorporating griseofulvin into directly compressed tablets containing a variety of excipient combinations. Across all formulations, the presence of griseofulvin significantly reduced wettability and maximum swelling size, consistent with replacing hygroscopic excipients with a poorly soluble, hydrophobic drug. Bayesian hierarchical modelling confirmed credible decreases in swelling capacity for all formulations and formulation-dependent changes in initial swelling rate. Notably, MCC/lactose tablets exhibited faster initial swelling and shorter disintegration times despite reduced porosity, suggesting API-induced microstructural changes that enhance access of liquid to the swellable excipients. Overall, the proposed framework provides a rapid (<6 min), mechanistic and minimally subjective method for probing formulation-dependent disintegration behaviour. For griseofulvin, the method was sensitive to changes in absorption and swelling behaviour, highlighting its potential as a high-throughput formulation screening approach. Further studies involving a wider range of APIs are needed to determine whether these observations are generalisable and relevant to disintegration and dissolution performance.

articles.title: Scale-independent prediction of ribbon and granule quality in dry granulation process based on transfer learning for process transfer.
articles.abstract: In dry granulation, differences in equipment geometry, compaction mechanisms, and powder flow behavior prevent quality prediction models based on a single device from achieving cross-scale and cross-equipment predictions of ribbon solid fraction (SF) and granule quality. Focusing on ten traditional Chinese medicine "Jichuan decoction" extracts, this study proposes a hybrid transfer learning (TL) framework to perform two-level device transfer for scale-independent prediction of ribbon and granule quality. In the first transfer level, a source domain dataset is constructed using uniaxial compaction experiments, and a target domain dataset using roller compaction experiments; material compression characteristics are extracted via the Johanson model. T-shaped partial least squares regression (T-PLSR) is then introduced for feature alignment and knowledge transfer. In the second transfer level, a Johanson + T-PLSR hybrid model is built, using the compression parameters output by the physical model as input features to jointly predict ribbon solid fraction and density, granule yield, and friability. This hybrid model overcomes the limitation of the Johanson model, which only predicts ribbon solid fraction, achieving end-to-end prediction from material compaction behavior to final granule quality. Validation results show that the prediction accuracy of the hybrid transfer model is significantly superior to pure physical or pure data-driven models, while the inclusion of physical parameters enhances model interpretability and generalization ability.

articles.title: A multifunctional injectable, adhesive and self-healing carboxymethyl cellulose/alginate hydrogel reinforced with clove oil-caseinate nanoparticles for diabetic wound healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wound healing is frequently impaired by a persistently inflammatory wound microenvironment accompanied by impaired angiogenesis. Therefore, fabrication of advanced wound dressings to restore a favorable wound microenvironment is essential to accelerate the healing process. This study developed a carboxymethyl cellulose/sodium alginate (CMC/ALG) hydrogel reinforced with clove oil-loaded sodium caseinate nanoparticle (CO-CAS NPs) as a wound dressing with multifunctional properties for diabetic wound repair. Clove oil was extracted by hydro-distillation and characterized by GC-MS, revealing eugenol and β-caryophyllene as the principal constituents. The fabricated CO-CAS NPs exhibited EE of 82%, with surface charge of - 40.47 mV and hydrodynamic size of 330.4 nm. The CO-CAS NPs/CMC/ALG hydrogel exhibited superior swelling capacity, reduced degradation, sustained release, and favorable mechanical properties, including injectability, stretchability, moldability, and autonomous self-healing behavior. In vivo, CO-CAS NPs/CMC/ALG hydrogel significantly accelerated wound contraction, as wounds achieved complete closure by day 18, versus 91% in the blank hydrogel group. Histopathological analyses demonstrated that treatment with the CO-CAS NPs/CMC/ALG hydrogel promoted re-epithelialization, fibroblast proliferation, and collagen fiber organization. These findings were supported by significant suppression of IL-6 and oxidative stress markers, as well as significant upregulation of TGF-β and VEGF, reflecting improved tissue remodeling and angiogenesis. In vivo biocompatibility assessments confirmed excellent dermal safety with no irritation or histopathological changes. These findings collectively demonstrate that CO-CAS NPs/CMC/ALG hydrogel is an effective, biocompatible, and multifunctional dressing for diabetic skin wounds.

articles.title: Spermacoce stachydea DC. (Rubiaceae), a Traditionally Used Antimalarial Plant: Phytochemical Profiling, Antioxidant and Antiplasmodial Activities, Host-Protective Effects, and Preclinical Safety Assessment.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Spermacoce stachydea (Rubiaceae) is traditionally used for malaria treatment across West Africa, yet its phytochemical composition, antioxidant properties, antiplasmodial activity, and safety profile remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive preclinical characterisation for its ethnomedicinal use in malaria management. METHODS: The whole-plant methanolic extract was profiled by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Total phenolic (TPC), flavonoid (TFC), and condensed tannin (CTC) contents were quantified, and antioxidant capacity was assessed by 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP), and oxygen radical absorbance capacity (ORAC) assays. Antiplasmodial activity was evaluated in vitro against Plasmodium falciparum 3D7 using a growth inhibition assay and in vivo in Plasmodium berghei ANKA-mice using a four-day suppressive test at 125, 250, and 500 mg/kg b.wt., and curative and prophylactic models at 250 mg/kg b.wt. Host-protective effects defined as the capacity of the extract to attenuate malaria-induced physiological disturbances including anaemia, organ enlargement, and hepatic and renal dysfunction were evaluated at 250 mg/kg b.wt. through restorative and protective assays encompassing physiological, haematological, biochemical analyses. Safety was assessed following single oral administration at 2000 and 5000 mg/kg b.wt. and repeated oral administration at 20, 200, and 2000 mg/kg b.wt./day in accordance with Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) guidelines 423 and 407, respectively. RESULTS: Phytochemical profiling revealed a diverse array of bioactive metabolites including flavonoids, terpenoids, coumarins, iridoids, alkaloids, and polyphenols. The extract exhibited a flavonoid-dominant phenolic profile (TPC: 33.99 ± 0.07 mg GAE/100 mg; TFC: 7.57 ± 0.03 mg QE/100 mg) and strong DPPH radical-scavenging activity reached 774 ± 3.9 μmol AAE/g, compared with 647 ± 3.5 and 766 ± 2.9 μmol AAE/g for Trolox and quercetin, respectively. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was significant (IC50 = 6.30 ± 0.13 μg/mL) with negligible haemolysis (<1%). In vivo, parasitaemia suppression reached 88.10 ± 6 % at 500 mg/kg (suppressive model), with good curative (58.40 ± 14.70%) and moderate prophylactic (35.70 ± 5.60%) activities at 250 mg/kg b.wt.. The extract attenuated malaria-associated physiological disturbances including anaemia, organ enlargement, and hepatic and renal dysfunction while demonstrated hepatoprotective effects. No mortality or consistent treatment-related toxicological alterations were observed after a single oral dose up to 5000 mg/kg b.wt. or repeated administration up to 2000 mg/kg b.wt./day. The median lethal dose exceeded 5000 mg/kg b.wt., and the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 2000 mg/kg b.wt./day under the study conditions. CONCLUSION: S. stachydea demonstrated significant antiplasmodial, antioxidant, and host-protective activities with a favourable safety profile, providing preliminary scientific support for its traditional use in malaria management and identifying it as a promising candidate for bioassay-guided investigation of its active constituents.

articles.title: Evaluation of PRG4 mRNA-Loaded Polymeric Nanoparticles in In Vitro and In Vivo Models of Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a highly prevalent degenerative joint disease for which no disease-modifying treatments are available. Proteoglycan 4 (PRG4) is a glycoprotein with lubricating and immunomodulatory properties, making it a promising therapeutic target for mRNA-based therapies. Therefore, this study evaluated the effects of PRG4 mRNA delivered via polymeric nanoparticles in both in vitro and in vivo OA models. METHODS: Human chondrocytes from OA patients were cultured in 3D pellet models and transfected with PRG4 mRNA-loaded polymeric nanoparticles at low or high dose, once or twice, respectively. Viability, pellet growth, glycosaminoglycan (GAG) production and mRNA expression were assessed, with EGFP mRNA transfection as a negative control. In vivo, an osteoarthritis rat model was used to evaluate PRG4 mRNA effects on pain behavior, cartilage degeneration, and synovial inflammation. RESULTS: In vitro, nanoparticle treatment induced an increase in pellet size and overall GAG production, independent of their cargo. PRG4 mRNA nanoparticle treatment at lower doses increased total pellet GAG content and early GAG release. Higher doses showed no additional benefit, and repeated transfection of the high dose significantly decreased cell viability. Double transfection of either dose showed increased relative expression of PRG4 mRNA, indicating uptake of the nanoparticles into the pellet. In vivo, PRG4 mRNA nanoparticles did not alleviate pain, reduce OA severity, or mitigate synovial inflammation. Sham-operated joints injected with mRNA-loaded nanoparticles showed increased OA and inflammation scores compared to healthy joints. CONCLUSIONS: MRNA-loaded nanoparticles increased extracellular matrix production in vitro independent of mRNA sequence. A minor effect of delivering PRG4 mRNA compared to control mRNA was found in matrix production normalized to cell content, but this was not reproduced in vivo. An intrinsic effect of nanoparticles on matrix production is suggested. Further research into the biodistribution of the presented nanoparticles and their cellular uptake into the different joint tissues is necessary for the advancement of mRNA-based treatments of OA.

articles.title: Ubiquitin-Like protein UBL1 orchestrates monocyte recruitment and pro-inflammatory macrophage activation in critical limb ischemia: Involving SUMOylation and stabilization of PER1.
articles.abstract: Critical limb ischemia (CLI), a severe manifestation of peripheral artery disease (PAD), is marked by accumulation of pro-inflammatory monocytes (Mos) and macrophages (Mφs) in ischemic skeletal muscles. Ubiquitin-Like Protein UBL1, an effector of small ubiquitin-like modifier mediated modification (SUMOylation), has been implicated in Mo/Mφ-associated tissue inflammation. However, the role of UBL1 in CLI has not been fully investigated. In this study, UBL1 expression was downregulated in peripheral blood Mos from CLI patients, and from hind limb ischemia (HLI) mice induced by femoral artery ligation (FAL). Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated UBL1 knockdown (KD) in HIL mice hindered blood flow recovery, aggravated tissue injury, and induced pro-inflammatory Mφ activation. Moreover, UBL1 KD reduced period circadian regulator 1 (PER1) expression in peripheral blood Mos isolated from HLI mice. UBL1 promoted PER1 SUMOylation at lysine 146 (K146) site, thereby enhancing its protein stability. Hypoxia significantly inhibited this process, with ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 I (UBE2I) being critically involved. Additionally, UBL1 KD promoted hypoxia-induced Mo migration via C-C Chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2) signaling and advanced pro-inflammatory cytokine release from hypoxic THP-1 derived Mφs. More importantly, rescue assays demonstrated that PER1 mediated UBL1 KD-induced Mo migration and pro-inflammatory Mφ activation. In summary, this study highlights the significance of UBL1 in HLI via regulating PER1 SUMOylation.

articles.title: Basis of the IgM cleavage activity of IgMDELsp and IgMDEMma.
articles.abstract: Abnormally elevated immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels can cause tissue damage and increase susceptibility to bacterial infections. Therefore, the use of IgM-degrading enzymes is clinically important for treating diseases characterized by elevated IgM levels. IgMDELsp and IgMDEMma are two newly discovered highly specific IgM-degrading enzymes. Here, we resolved the crystal structures of IgMDELsp and IgMDEMma. Despite their highly conserved structure, the activity level of IgMDELsp is significantly greater than that of IgMDEMma. By predicting their complexes with the IgM substrate, we deduced the potential reasons for their substantial activity disparity. IgMDELsp exhibits high IgM-cleaving activity through triplet catalysis. We inferred the potential reasons for their vastly differing activities by predicting their complexes with the IgM substrate. IgMDELsp exhibits high IgM cleavage activity through its catalytic triad. However, IgMDEMma exists in multiple polymeric states, particularly dimers, in which spatial steric effects arise during substrate recognition. These dimers interfere with IgM Fc through spatial conflicts, partially hindering binding and IgM cleavage via the catalytic triad, which likely underlies its significantly lower activity than IgMDELsp. We subsequently validated the in vivo activity of IgMDELsp in mice. Overall, the structural elucidation of these novel IgM-degrading enzymes provides potential therapeutic targets for diseases characterized by elevated IgM levels.

articles.title: Thymoquinone alleviates DSS-induced colitis in mice by protecting the intestinal mucosal barrier through inhibition of the Notch signalling pathway.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the therapeutic effects and potential molecular mechanisms of the natural plant monomer thymoquinone (TQ) on colitis in mice. Particular attention was paid to protecting intestinal barrier integrity, apoptosis, and inflammatory responses. METHODS: Colitis was induced in mice using 3% Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS). Concurrently, TQ (20 and 80 mg/kg) was administered intragastrically from days 1 to 7. The development of colitis and intestinal barrier integrity were assessed by monitoring body weight, Disease Activity Index (DAI) score, colonic length changes, pathological alterations, inflammatory cytokines, and the expression of relevant proteins. Caco-2 cells were stimulated in vitro with 100 ng/ml TNF-α to validate the regulatory effects of TQ on the Notch signaling pathway and tight junction proteins. RESULTS: TQ significantly alleviates DSS-induced histopathological damage in mouse colon tissue, lowering the DAI. It reduces levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β) in peripheral serum, increases levels of the anti-inflammatory factor IL-10, and upregulates expression of intestinal barrier proteins (ZO-1, Occludin, MUC2). Furthermore, TQ upregulated Bcl-2, downregulated Bax, inhibited the activation of Cleaved Caspase-3, and reduced the apoptosis of mouse colonic epithelial cells. Mechanistically, TQ suppressed the excessive activation of the Notch signaling pathway, which is consistent with the results of the in vitro experiments. CONCLUSION: TQ significantly alleviated the clinical manifestations and pathological damage in DSS-induced colitis in mice, protected the integrity of intestinal epithelial cells, and reduced apoptosis, demonstrating its potential as a novel therapeutic agent for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

articles.title: Luteolin as a potential intervention for bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis: targeting the AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α/MMP2 axis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a life-threatening interstitial lung disease that endangers human health. Luteolin (LUT), a naturally occurring flavonoid, has exhibited potential effects against pulmonary fibrosis. However, its mechanism of action remains unclear. Here, we investigated the therapeutic effects of LUT against PF and explored its underlying molecular mechanisms. Bioinformatics analysis was used to predict LUT targets. PF was induced in mice via a single intratracheal instillation of bleomycin (BLM). The effects of LUT were evaluated using histopathology, Western blotting, real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and immunofluorescence. HIF-1α siRNA interference was used for mechanistic validation. The experimental findings revealed that bioinformatics prediction highlighted the HIF-1 signaling pathway. LUT significantly alleviated BLM-induced lung injury and suppressed epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix deposition. Mechanistically, LUT downregulated the expression of AKT, mTOR, HIF-1α, and MMP2. The siRNA knockdown of HIF-1α confirmed its central role. This study demonstrates that LUT ameliorates PF by modulating the AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α/MMP2 axis, providing novel evidence for the structural verification of this specific signaling cascade and supporting its potential as an agent for lung health.

articles.title: Gallic acid attenuates PTSD-like behavioral and hippocampal neuroplasticity deficits induced by single prolonged stress in male rats.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with persistent cognitive and emotional disturbances linked to hippocampal dysfunction, oxidative stress, and impaired neuroplasticity. Gallic acid, a naturally occurring polyphenol, possesses antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, but its effects in trauma-related disorders remain incompletely understood. Male Wistar rats were subjected to single prolonged stress (SPS) to induce PTSD-like phenotypes and, beginning 24 h after SPS, received gallic acid (10 or 100 mg/kg) or saline for 14 days. Anxiety-like behavior, fear extinction, and spatial learning and memory were assessed using the elevated plus maze, contextual fear conditioning with extinction, and Morris water maze, respectively. Hippocampal oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, and TAC), BDNF protein expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology were evaluated. SPS exposure induced anxiety-like behavior, impaired fear extinction, and deficits in spatial learning and memory, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, reduced antioxidant capacity, decreased hippocampal BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic atrophy. Early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuated these behavioral alterations and was accompanied by improvements in hippocampal oxidative status, BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology, without detectable effects on locomotor activity or relative adrenal gland weight. Collectively, these findings indicate that early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuates SPS-associated behavioral and hippocampal abnormalities and that these effects are associated with antioxidant and neuroplasticity-related changes rather than establishing a causal mechanism. Further studies using delayed treatment paradigms and pathway-specific approaches are needed to determine the efficacy of gallic acid after establishment of the PTSD-like phenotype and to clarify the mechanisms underlying its effects.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine decreases toluene conditioned place preference and modulates corticostriatal activity in adolescent rats.
articles.abstract: Inhalant (toluene) use disorder (IUD) continues to be a public health problem especially among Filipino adolescents. Animal models of IUD have not explored neurobiological changes from chronic toluene exposure, or possible treatments for long-lasting toluene-induced deficits. In rats repeatedly exposed to 3000 ppm of toluene vapor over 12 days, we report that daily administration of N-acetylcysteine (NAC; 100 mg/kg i.p. or 0.9 g/l oral), but not melatonin (10 mg/kg i.p.), during 8 days of abstinence reduced toluene conditioned place preference in both male and female adolescent Sprague-Dawley rats. Using immunofluorescence, we found that toluene-exposed rats showed decreased c-Fos densities in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), dorsolateral striatum, and ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex (vlOFC) after 8 days of abstinence. NAC partially rescued c-Fos expression in vlOFC. We found that c-Fos densities in both vlOFC and prelimbic cortex were significantly correlated with CPP values and with c-Fos densities in the DMS across treatment groups, suggesting that a history of toluene exposure may act by reducing cortical modulation of the dorsal striatum to promote long-lasting drug context-seeking. Our findings suggest that N-acetylcysteine may be a promising treatment for IUD in adolescent males and females.

articles.title: ELF1 exacerbates intervertebral disc degeneration by promoting ACSL4-dependent ferro-aging of nucleus pulposus cells through the IFITM3-PTPRO axis.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain and is characterized by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence and extracellular matrix degradation. Ferro-aging, a chronic iron-dependent lipid peroxidation-associated senescence program, has recently been proposed as a potential mechanism linking metabolic dysregulation with tissue aging. However, whether ferro-aging contributes to IVDD and how it is regulated remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of ferro-aging in IVDD and identify its upstream regulatory network. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, human nucleus pulposus tissue validation, puncture-induced and age-related IVDD animal models, and multiple NPC senescence models were used to investigate IFITM3-associated ferro-aging. Loss- and gain-of-function approaches, RNA sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays were performed to investigate the regulatory network involving ELF1, IFITM3, PTPRO, and ACSL4. KEY FINDINGS: IFITM3 showed increased expression in degenerated NPCs and was associated with ferroptosis-related pathways, inflammatory responses, and extracellular matrix remodeling. IFITM3 promoted NPC ferro-aging by enhancing iron accumulation, ACSL4 expression, lipid peroxidation, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence. Mechanistically, PTPRO was identified as an IFITM3-associated regulatory node that contributes to ACSL4 protein stabilization and lipid peroxidation, while ELF1 transcriptionally activates IFITM3. Genetic inhibition of Ifitm3, Ptpro, or Elf1 alleviated ferro-aging phenotypes and attenuated IVDD progression. SIGNIFICANCE: This study identifies ferro-aging as a previously unrecognized mechanism contributing to IVDD and identifies a regulatory network involving ELF1, IFITM3, PTPRO, and ACSL4 as a potential therapeutic framework for delaying disc degeneration.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota Remodeling Correlates with Pentose Phosphate Pathway Activation and Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis Dysregulation in Polystyrene Nanoplastic-Induced Hepatic Lipotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) have been detected in human tissues, but the systemic consequences of chronic oral exposure remain unclear. Female Sprague-Dawley rats received environmentally relevant PS-NP concentrations of 5 or 50 mg/L in drinking water for 42 days. Gut-liver-endocrine interactions were assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, fecal metabolomics, hepatic transcriptomics, and biochemical validation of selected nodes. PS-NP exposure caused notable dysregulation of serum and hepatic lipids and produced histopathological damage in the liver. The exposure was also associated with gut dysbiosis dominated by Bacteroidia, along with hepatic glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) upregulation and pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) activation, as well as NADPH accumulation. Low-dose exposure was associated with adaptive redox responses (elevated hepatic superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-PX)) and lipid clearance signatures, whereas high-dose exposure correlated with GSH-PX depletion, elevated 8-iso-prostaglandin (8-iso-PG), and transcriptomic evidence of mitochondrial impairment and ferroptosis vulnerability. Steroid hormone biosynthesis (SHB) disruption-declining estradiol and rising cortisol-was observed across both doses, with ovarian Cyp19a1/Cyp11a1 downregulation at low dose and additional adrenal Cyp21a2 upregulation at high dose. Multi-omics integration linked Bacteroidia enrichment to the PPP intermediate deoxyribose 5-phosphate and to reduced estrogen metabolites. Collectively, these findings outline a Gut Microbiota-PPP-SHB (GMPS) axis as a candidate integrative framework for understanding PS-NP-associated hepatic lipotoxicity. This work offers an integrative resource that identifies candidate pathways and testable hypotheses for future investigation of metabolic risks from chronic nanoplastic exposure.

articles.title: C5aR2 signaling mechanisms via the β-arrestin-dependent pathway observed in microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations.
articles.abstract: The complement system primarily regulates innate immunity, contributing to nonspecific antipathogen defense, and is linked to adaptive immunity. One of its components, C5 convertase, initiates the last stage of the complement cascade, leading to the cleavage of C5 into C5a and C5b and the formation of the membrane attack complex, which causes cell lysis. In addition, C5a acts as a proinflammatory mediator by regulating leukocyte chemotaxis. C5a binds to 2 G protein-coupled receptors: C5aR1 and C5aR2. C5aR1 activation is involved in inflammation through both G protein and β-arrestin-mediated signaling, while the effects of C5a binding to C5aR2 evoking only the β-arrestin signaling pathway are less defined. C5aR2, often considered a decoy receptor, exhibits both proinflammatory and anti-inflammatory effects in various disease models. To elucidate the physiological significance and therapeutic potential of C5aR2 signaling, we performed 4 μs-scale molecular dynamics simulations of the C5a-C5aR2-β-arrestin 1 complex starting from the active-state β-arrestin conformation. Two possible helix 8 (H8) conformations found in Protein Data Bank structures of C5aR1 used as templates for C5aR2 were tested. The canonical, outward-directed H8, lacking an amphipathic amino acid composition, untangled in all simulations. The noncanonical, inverted conformation of H8 remained stable in these 4-μs-long simulations, with a slight, incomplete clockwise rotation and the simultaneous outward movement of TM7, as observed in sweet-taste G protein-coupled receptors. Nevertheless, in both simulation systems, a short hydrophobic H8 fragment (LPAA) formed a stable anchor to the lipid bilayer throughout the 4-μs simulation. Based on our observations, we suggest that H8 could be limited to this short helical hydrophobic LPAA anchor that stabilizes the active-state β-arrestin conformation. These findings may explain the distinct, non-G protein-mediated signaling of C5aR2 compared with C5aR1 and provide insights into the 2 C5a-mediated signaling pathways, which exhibit significantly different therapeutic potential in the treatment of inflammatory diseases. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This extensive 4-μs-long, 6-replica molecular dynamics study provides important insights into the molecular basis of C5aR2 signaling, which can lead to either proinflammatory or anti-inflammatory effects, and could be exploited in the treatment of inflammatory diseases. To best of the authors' knowledge, it is the first study to present the molecular determinants of β-arrestin-biased signaling in the C5aR2 system. In addition, it elucidates the molecular mechanisms underlying β-arrestin-mediated signaling, focusing on its conformations and interactions with the receptor.

articles.title: Interleukin-37 overexpression enhances the therapeutic efficacy of adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells in atopic dermatitis by activating autophagy and improving skin barrier dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADSCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic option because of their immunomodulatory and tissue-repair capabilities in the treatment of Atopic dermatitis (AD). However, their efficacy is limited by cellular senescence and functional decline. Interleukin-37 (IL-37), an anti-inflammatory cytokine, has shown potential in mitigating inflammation and enhancing skin barrier function. This study investigated whether IL-37 overexpression in ADSCs could augment their therapeutic effects in AD and the underlying mechanism. Lentiviral-mediated IL-37 overexpression in ADSCs enhanced proliferation, reduced senescence (evidenced by decreased β-galactosidase activity), and activated autophagy, as shown by elevated LC3B-II/I and Beclin-1 levels, reduced p62, and increased LC3B puncta formation. These effects were reversed by the autophagy inhibitor 3-MA. In an IL-4/IL-13-induced HaCaT cell model of AD, coculture with IL-37-overexpressing ADSCs promoted keratinocyte proliferation, reduced apoptosis, suppressed proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine), and restored the expression of skin barrier proteins (Filaggrin, Involucrin). In vivo, local injection of IL-37-overexpressing ADSCs into lesional skin in a 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene-induced AD mouse model attenuated skin lesions, reduced inflammation, and improved barrier protein expression. These results demonstrate that IL-37 overexpression enhances the therapeutic efficacy of ADSCs in AD through autophagy activation and restoration of skin barrier function, providing a novel genetically engineered stem cell-based strategy for the treatment of AD. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: IL-37-engineered adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells improve atopic dermatitis treatment by activating autophagy to reduce senescence and enhance proliferation. These cells suppress inflammation while restoring skin barrier proteins, providing a novel therapy for refractory skin diseases.

articles.title: Sex-specific exploration patterns and noradrenergic modulation in object recognition memory: Role of the perirhinal cortex.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Object recognition memory (ORM) relies on two processes: familiarity, mediated by the perirhinal cortex (PRH), and recollection, supported by the hippocampus (HIP). These processes are recruited depending on memory strength: brief exploration forms weak traces relying on PRH familiarity, whereas extended exploration produces strong traces requiring HIP recollection. Noradrenaline (NA) modulates these mechanisms via β2-adrenergic receptors (β2-AR), influencing memory strength and consolidation. However, whether this modulation differs between sexes under conditions generating weak versus strong memory traces remains unknown. We examined how NA and β2-AR influence ORM in male and female mice under these conditions. METHODS: Swiss mice were tested in the Novel Object Recognition task using training durations of 1-10 min and delays of 24-48 h. Atomoxetine (ATO) was used to increase NA levels, and ICI-118,551 (ICI) to block β2-AR. Neural activation was assessed via c-Fos immunohistochemistry in PRH and HIP. RESULTS: Females showed greater efficiency in object processing, requiring less exploration than males. Under weak training conditions, ATO facilitated the formation of long-term ORM in females but not in males, accompanied by increased PRH c-Fos expression without HIP involvement. β2-AR blockade impaired ORM acquisition only in females, with no significant changes in c-Fos. In males, performance depended on object dissimilarity; increased NA did not enhance ORM unless stimuli were highly distinct. CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal sex differences in noradrenergic modulation of ORM. In females, NA acting via β2-AR supports memory formation through PRH-dependent familiarity, emphasizing the importance of sex as a biological variable in research.

articles.title: pH-responsive hydrogel delivery of Lycium barbarum glycopeptide coordinates immune-matrix crosstalk to enhance wound healing.
articles.abstract: Advanced wound dressings should combine physical protection with localized and microenvironment-responsive delivery of therapeutic agents. Lycium barbarum glycopeptide (LbGp), a naturally derived macromolecular preparation with reported immunomodulatory and tissue-protective activities; however, its topical use is limited by rapid diffusion and insufficient local retention. Here, we engineered an injectable oxidized sodium alginate/gelatin hydrogel (OSA/Gel@LbGp) for localized delivery of LbGp through dynamic Schiff-base crosslinking. OSA/Gel@LbGp showed favorable cytocompatibility, promoted HaCaT keratinocyte migration, and shifted LPS-challenged macrophages toward a repair-associated phenotype, as evidenced by reduced CD68, TNF-α, and IL-1β and increased CD206, ARG-1, and TGF-β1. In a murine 5-mm full-thickness excisional wound model, OSA/Gel@LbGp accelerated wound closure, reduced granulation-tissue gaps, enhanced re-epithelialization, and improved dermal organization and collagen deposition. RNA sequencing subsequently identified 2,097 upregulated and 980 downregulated genes, revealing an ECM-centered reparative program enriched in ECM-receptor interaction, cell-matrix adhesion, and matrix-remodeling pathways, with Mmp11 emerging as a representative remodeling-associated gene. Consistent with this transcriptional findings, treated wound tissues exhibited increased collagen I/COL1A1, MMP11, and VEGF signals,and reduced inflammation-linked MMP9. Collectively, OSA/Gel@LbGp promoted wound repair by coordinating early immune modulation with subsequent ECM reconstruction. These findings establish a delivery-centered strategy for translating natural macromolecular bioactives into advanced wound dressings that improve both healing kinetics and tissue-repair quality.

articles.title: Telepharmacological Consultation for Polypharmacy Management in Primary Care: A Qualitative Study of General Practitioners' Experiences With Cross-Sectoral Coordination.
articles.abstract: The telepharmacological outpatient clinic (TPOC) is a hospital service in which clinical pharmacologists and clinical pharmacists review a patient's full medication regimen and hospital record, then discuss it with the referring general practitioner (GP) by video conference. Seven GPs in the Region of Southern Denmark who had used or been introduced to the service were interviewed to explore how it was used and what prevented wider use. Interviews were semi-structured and analysed thematically. GPs described practices organised around single diagnoses, with no separate pathway for patients who are difficult because they are complex. This was the setting the service entered. Four themes were identified. Whether the service was used depended on integration into existing clinical software. Its value reached past the referred patient, as GPs applied what they had learned to patients never referred. GPs described a coordination gap for patients attending several outpatient clinics, where no clinician held an overview of the whole treatment. They wanted the intensity of the service matched to the complexity of the case. GPs who wanted to refer more often pointed to awareness and time pressure, not to doubts about the service. Uptake appears to depend on workflow integration.

articles.title: Stroboscopic light stimulation as a controllable probe of the psilocybin state: a mechanistic framework and a falsifiable prediction.
articles.abstract: Stroboscopic light stimulation (SLS) and psilocybin each induce altered states whose phenomenology and neurophysiology partly overlap, including posterior alpha-band changes and visual imagery. The two states engage the alpha band through different operations - pharmacological suppression under psilocybin and frequency-selective visual drive under SLS. We formalize their possible interaction for prediction and falsification. The framework proposes that, by relaxing the precision weighting of high-level cortical priors and, through 5-HT2A activation, suppressing posterior alpha-band power, psilocybin creates a state in which an exogenous, frequency-controlled visual rhythm can modulate the perceiver's experience. The thesis concerns precision rather than response amplitude. Because existing neuroimaging comes mostly from eyes-closed rest, where directional evidence is contested, the falsification does not depend on which sensory-inclusive model, Relaxed Beliefs Under Psychedelics (REBUS) or cortico-striatal-thalamo-cortical (CSTC), is correct. The framework predicts that, within a prespecified near-peak psilocin window, rhythmic SLS raises the Visionary Restructuralization dimension of the five-dimensional Altered States of Consciousness questionnaire (5D-ASC) relative to a luminance- and rate-matched arrhythmic control - an increase a precision framework predicts even if evoked amplitude does not rise. A complementary, report-independent endpoint, the intermodulation response to two-frequency stimulation, is proposed. State-dependence is tested as the drug-by-rhythmicity interaction in a 2 × 3 factorial design (placebo or psilocybin × rhythmic SLS, arrhythmic control, or no stimulation), with the sign of any interaction evaluated on a pre-declared scale. An adequately precise negative interaction would count against the central state-dependence prediction for the tested conditions. The framework organizes five axes around this prediction: titration of experiential intensity at fixed dose, content shaping through frequency specificity, modulation of difficult-experience phenomenology, testing whether resting-state signatures depend on sensory context, and individual-difference profiling of SLS responsiveness. The framework makes no claim of therapeutic enhancement. Its aim is mechanistic and methodological.

articles.title: Dynamic kinetics of graft-derived cell-free DNA and personalized tacrolimus target ranges for acute rejection monitoring in pediatric liver transplantation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute rejection remains the most common complication during the early post-transplantation period for pediatric patients. Given the limitations of current diagnostic strategies, there is an urgent need to develop accurate and noninvasive biomarkers for allograft monitoring. Tacrolimus-based immunosuppression represents the cornerstone regimen following liver transplantation. However, for pediatric patients, current evidence remains insufficient to establish well-defined therapeutic target ranges for personalized tacrolimus therapy in pediatric patients. We investigated perioperative graft-derived cell-free DNA (GcfDNA) kinetics in pediatric recipients to establish the utility of GcfDNA for monitoring acute rejection and to explore the tacrolimus target concentration range in this population. METHODS: Forty children (age ≤ 3 years) with biliary atresia who underwent liver transplantation were enrolled. All received a tacrolimus-based immunosuppressive regimen on postoperative day (POD) 1 and were followed for at least 1 month. GcfDNA levels were measured by droplet digital PCR. RESULTS: GcfDNA (%) declined significantly during the first month. Median percentages on POD 1, 7, 14, 21, and 28 were 41.40%, 12.93%, 6.86%, 5.95%, and 3.23%, respectively. The acute rejection group maintained higher GcfDNA levels, with significant differences observed at POD 14, 21, and 28 (P < 0.001). GcfDNA (%) was strongly correlated with rejection activity index score (r = 0.854, P < 0.001). In this exploratory single-center analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis identified an optimal GcfDNA cutoff of 10.21% for predicting acute rejection, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.757 (95% CI: 0.691-0.823, P < 0.001). The optimal tacrolimus trough concentration (C0) threshold was 7.75 ng/mL (AUC = 0.732, 95% CI: 0.655-0.810, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: We suggest that GcfDNA may serve as a potential biomarker for acute rejection monitoring in pediatric liver transplantation, with an exploratory predictive cutoff value of 10.21% identified in this single-center cohort. Our findings also tentatively point to a minimal effective tacrolimus C0 of 7.75 ng/mL within the first month post-transplantation, alongside an upper safety limit of 10 ng/mL that is primarily grounded in published peer-reviewed literatures. These thresholds, however, were optimized against stable grafts rather than the full spectrum of graft injury and require multicenter validation before clinical adoption.

articles.title: Adjunctive Acorus tatarinowii essential-oil ear-canal packing for idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss: study protocol for a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL) is an acute otologic emergency, and hearing recovery remains highly variable and frequently unsatisfactory. Acorus tatarinowii Schott has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to treat hearing impairment and related auditory disorders. Its essential oil (SCP-oil) has demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective activities in preclinical studies. Advances in local otologic drug-delivery strategies suggest that administration through the external auditory canal may offer a practical, noninvasive approach to local treatment. This study therefore aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing in patients with ISSNHL. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to be conducted at Zhejiang Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine. The trial has been registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR2026000919). A total of 258 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive conventional therapy combined with either SCP-oil ear-canal packing or glycerin placebo ear-canal packing for 14 consecutive days. The primary outcome is the study-defined total markedly effective rate of hearing recovery at week 2, defined as the proportion of participants achieving complete recovery or marked improvement, as assessed by pure-tone audiometry. Secondary outcomes include the mean improvement in hearing thresholds across the affected frequencies, the hearing-recovery categories, tinnitus severity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), depressive symptoms assessed using the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), and sleep quality assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Efficacy outcomes will be assessed at baseline and week 2, with an additional safety assessment conducted at week 4. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study. DISCUSSION: This trial will provide evidence on the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing for ISSNHL, including its effects on hearing recovery and patient-reported outcomes. The findings may also inform the design of future multicenter clinical trials.

articles.title: Phenolic metabolites from Ceratonia siliqua L. pods: chemical characterization, soybean lipoxygenase-1 inhibition, and in vitro gallstone-dissolving capacity.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Carob (Ceratonia siliqua L., Fabaceae) is a Mediterranean tree whose pods are rich in phenolic metabolites and are credited with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory,hypolipidemic and antimicrobial properties. METHODS: The chemical composition of MECp was determined by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with ultraviolet detection (HPLC/UV). Free radical-scavenging and ferric-reducing capacities were measured using the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) and ferric-reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) analytical descriptors assays, and soybean LOX-1 inhibition was assessed in vitro and examined in silico by molecular docking against the enzyme (PDB ID: 3O8Y). Gallstones removed at surgery were confirmed as cholesterol stones by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy with attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) and then incubated in MECp under continuous agitation for 4 weeks, with a sodium chloride solution (NaCl, 9 g/L) as control. Gallstone mass after drying at 40 °C, the percentage of gallstone-dissolving capacity (% GDC) and the pH of the medium were recorded weekly. RESULTS: HPLC/UV analysis identified 20 phenolic metabolites in MECp. The extract contained 160.68 mg GAE/g DE of total phenolics and 9.19 mg QE/g DE of total flavonoids, with median inhibitory concentrations (IC50) of 0.16, 0.86 and 0.19 mg/mL for the DPPH, FRAP and soybean LOX-1 inhibition assays, respectively. Compared with the control, MECp produced a highly significant increase in % GDC over time, and the docking analysis revealed strong and stable interactions between the major polyphenols and the soybean LOX-1 active site. DISCUSSION: The dissolution obtained with MECp is consistent with its phenolic composition, and the docking results agree with the soybean LOX-1 inhibition measured in vitro. These findings identify MECp as a promising natural candidate for cholesterol gallstone management and support further preclinical investigation.

articles.title: Mapping the antileishmanial structure-activity relationship of eugenol.
articles.abstract: Leishmaniasis is a neglected tropical disease with a devastating global impact. The current medications on the market for treating this protozoan parasitic infection are insufficient to fit the global need, with long durations of therapy, growing resistance rates, and severe adverse effects. This investigation aims to characterize an antileishmanial structure-activity relationship for the natural product eugenol. With Leishmania donovani as a model, a series of dose-response curves were performed against eugenol and several of its structural analogs. The same set of compounds was tested against the human monocyte cell THP-1 to characterize their selective toxicity. Subsequently, the pharmacokinetic parameters of the tested compounds were estimated using the in silico modelling software, Percepta®. Eugenol and its analogs demonstrated varying levels of antileishmanial potency, with 4-allylphenol (chavicol) as the most potent compound tested and with the most promising selectivity index. In comparing the potencies and structures of the compounds tested, the data suggests that the para-substituted allyl tail and the phenolic group are important to conferring potency, while the ortho-methoxy substitutions decreased potency. Furthermore, the pharmacokinetic properties of these compounds were predicted to closely resemble eugenol with little risk of cytochrome P450 (CYP) interactions. While more testing is needed to confirm the mechanisms and safety of these compounds, these results suggest eugenol analogs show promise as future antileishmanial therapies.

articles.title: A pathway to next-generation mast cell stabilizers identified through the novel Phytomedical Analytics for Research Optimization at scale data platform.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mast cell stabilizers (MCS) have the potential to address unmet therapeutic need in allergy and inflammation management. MCS chronically suppress all arms of the pro-inflammatory mast cell response to stimulation (e.g., histamine, protease, lipid mediators, cytokines and chemokines). They may therefore outperform approaches such as H1, H2 and H4 inhibitors (antihistamines), which block only the acute histamine release by mast cells and leave the rest of the functional response untouched. Despite their potential, current MCS (e.g., cromolyn sodium, tranilast, nedocromil) in clinical use are hindered by poor bioavailability, frequent dosing, long lags to onset of relief, and enigmatic mechanisms of action. MCS have their origins in phytomedicine: cromolyn sodium is the longest standing drug in the class and is a derivatized form of khellin from Ammi visnaga, used as an anti-inflammatory. Other plant-based pharmacopeias may offer candidate 'next-generation' MCS (ngMCS) and in this study we hypothesized that a coupled pharmacoanalytic and in vitro pharmacology approach could be used to identify, prioritize and derisk additional candidate MCS from phytomedical sources for later preclinical and clinical evaluation. METHODS: We report a novel data analytics workflow starting with a newly developed plant-based pharmacopeia data platform with >3.5B linkage pathways (country → medical system → formulation → indication → ingredient organism → chemical component → other parameters), covering 22 M sq. miles of biogeography and historical and contemporary timeframes. Additional data layers include druggability indices, target and pathway analyses. RESULTS: The current study validates a subset of candidate phytomedical ngMCS using in silico workflow and in vitro pharmacology, and develops a new harmonic mean-based 'MCS score' for further streamlining of the candidate prioritization process. DISCUSSION: This proof-of-concept study may have particular relevance for complex presentations such as Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) where ngMCS may outperform current management approaches.

articles.title: Chicoric acid-rich extract of Cichorium intybus seeds (CAREOCI) preserves pancreatic β-cell function under glucotoxic stress through modulation of MAFA, DYRK1A, cell cycle, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Progressive decline in functional pancreatic β-cell mass is a key pathological feature of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), highlighting the need for therapies that preserve and regenerate β-cells. This study investigated the preservative effects of a chicoric acid-rich aqueous extract of Cichorium intybus seeds (CAREOCI) under glucotoxic conditions (25 mM glucose) in pancreatic β-cells. METHODS: Phytochemical standardisation by HPTLC, HPLC, and LC-MS/MS confirmed chicoric acid is the principal constituent present in CAREOCI. A molecular docking study identified DYRK1A is a one of the key target (-8.72 kcal/mol) of chicoric acid for β-cell regeneration. In glucotoxic MIN 6 β-cells, CAREOCI significantly enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, restored antioxidant status, reduced intracellular ROS, and suppressed IL-1β and TNF-α. RESULTS: CAREOCI also reduced apoptosis, attenuated caspase-3/7 activity, preserved normal nuclear morphology, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and promoted autophagy through increased acidic vesicular organelles. Cell-cycle analysis indicated a trend toward increased S-phase population, suggesting enhanced β-cell proliferation. At the molecular level, CAREOCI downregulated DYRK1A, NF-κB, mTOR, and CHOP while upregulating MAFA, PDX1, PAX6, and NKX6.1, supporting β-cell survival and preservation. Compared with purified chicoric acid, CAREOCI consistently exhibited greater efficacy, indicating potential complementarity among its phytoconstituents. CONCLUSION: CAREOCI protects pancreatic β-cells through coordinated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, mitochondrial-protective, autophagy-promoting effects, supporting beta cell preservation and function under glucotoxicity condition supporting its potential as a phytopharmaceutical for T2DM.

articles.title: Multimodal molecular representation and property prediction based on structured complementary feature fusion.
articles.abstract: In this work, we propose Molrep-SCF, a multimodal self-supervised pretraining framework for molecular representation learning using SMILES sequences, 2D molecular graphs, and 3D geometric structures. The three modalities are encoded using a Transformer, a graph neural network, and an invariant 3D graph neural network, respectively. To enrich geometric supervision beyond a single conformation, Molrep-SCF incorporates three selected and complementary 3D conformational views. We further introduce a 2D-guided conformational consistency refinement mechanism that uses molecular topology to guide the fusion and refinement of their geometric representations. Instead of relying on a single static conformation, our method enforces structural consistency across conformers under the guidance of 2D topological priors. Furthermore, we design a structure-aware cross-modal learning strategy with atomic-level alignment via position-specific masking, enabling fine-grained correspondence across modalities. In addition, masked reconstruction across modalities enhances deep semantic coupling and facilitates information exchange between heterogeneous representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Molrep-SCF consistently outperforms existing multi-modal frameworks on molecular property prediction and other tasks, showing stronger generalization and representation quality.

articles.title: Handling missed dose of riluzole by population pharmacokinetic model informed remedial regimen.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) frequently exhibit nonadherence characterized by delayed or missed doses while taking riluzole. This study aimed to provide a population pharmacokinetic (PPK) model informed individualized remedial regimens for patients who experience delayed or missed doses of riluzole. METHODS: A PPK model for riluzole was developed via a nonlinear mixed-effect modeling approach based on 3,024 concentration-time points from 72 subjects. The final model was validated by multiple methods. Six remedial regimens for missed doses were simulated for concentration-time profiles under different scenarios, and the optimal remedial regimen was selected based on the least time of concentration beyond the normal range. RESULTS: The PPK model of riluzole was best described with a two-compartment model with body weight as a covariate of peripheral distribution volume. The typical values of CL/F, Vc/F, Vp/F and Q were 67 L/h, 242 L, 376 L and 33.1 L/h, respectively. The model was showed acceptable performance by goodness-of-fit, visual predictive check, bootstrap analysis and normalized distribution prediction errors. Model-based remedial regimens for different missed scenarios were proposed. CONCLUSION: A riluzole PPK model was developed and internally evaluated using multiple diagnostic approaches. Model-based remedial dosing strategies for different missed-dose scenarios were identified based on predefined PK criteria and Monte Carlo simulations. These exploratory strategies provide quantitative insights into riluzole exposure during nonadherent dosing conditions.

articles.title: The postantibiotic effect-like effect of photothermal agents: evidence from IR780 nanoparticles and indocyanine green.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Postantibiotic effect (PAE) refers to the temporary suppression of bacterial growth after transient antimicrobial treatment. In recent years, due to the spread of antibiotic resistance, photothermal agents (PTAs) have been broadly studied for infection treatments. However, the PAE-like effect of PTAs has not been investigated. METHODS: This study focuses on the PAE-like effect of representative PTAs, namely IR780 nanoparticles (NPs) and indocyanine green (ICG), against MRSA and a CRE isolate. The effects of PTA type, bacterial species, PTA concentration, and near-infrared irradiation duration on the PAE-like effect were systematically evaluated. RESULTS: Results showed that the PAE-like effect of these PTAs against MRSA and a CRE isolate was evident. Further experiments showed that the PAE-like effect was affected by PTA type, bacterial species, PTA concentration, and near-infrared irradiation duration. Furthermore, the PAE-like effect of IR780 NPs was enhanced by 34.6% when a targeting group was conjugated to its nanostructure. DISCUSSION: The mechanism of the PAE-like effect of PTAs against MRSA is suggested to be related to thermally induced damage. Overall, this work provides the first evidence of a PAE-like effect in PTAs against MRSA, which may provide a preliminary basis for future optimization of photothermal therapy regimens against resistant infections.

articles.title: Apelin aggravates inflammatory response and hepatic steatosis in alcohol-associated liver disease via ERK signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Though apelin is involved in cardiovascular, metabolic, and homeostasis disorders, its role in alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of apelin in promoting hepatic inflammation in ALD. METHODS: RAW 264.7 macrophages and a chronic alcohol-fed C57BL/6 mouse model were used. Apelin activated ERK1/2 phosphorylation, and PD98059 pretreatment attenuated apelin-induced MCP-1 and PCNA expression. Inflammatory and proliferative markers (MCP-1, IL-6, PCNA) were assessed by qRT-PCR and western blot. ERK signaling was evaluated using the inhibitor PD98059. Liver pathology was examined by H&E and Oil Red O staining. RESULTS: Alcohol upregulated apelin expression in RAW 264.7 cells. Apelin-13 increased MCP-1 and PCNA expression in time- and dose-dependent manners. Apelin overexpression enhanced, while siRNA knockdown reduced, inflammatory and proliferative gene expression. Apelin activated ERK1/2 phosphorylation, and PD98059 pretreatment attenuated apelin-induced MCP-1 and PCNA expression. In vivo, apelin overexpression exacerbated steatosis, ballooning degeneration, and inflammatory infiltration, with elevated MCP-1, IL-6, and PCNA levels. CONCLUSION: Apelin aggravates inflammatory responses and hepatic steatosis in ALD via the ERK signaling pathway, suggesting that the apelin/APJ/p-ERK/inflammation axis may represent a novel therapeutic target for ALD.

articles.title: Electronic prescribing: Implementation of a new approach to undergraduate teaching and assessment.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Electronic prescribing and medicines administration (ePMA) systems are increasingly used across UK healthcare to reduce medication errors and improve patient safety. Undergraduate medical curricula have traditionally relied on handwritten prescribing, creating misalignment between education and clinical practice. To address this, the University of Manchester introduced electronic prescribing using the British Pharmacological Society (BPS) platform across its undergraduate medical programme. METHODS: This descriptive implementation (quality improvement) report outlines a curriculum change within a large undergraduate medical programme, structured using the ADDIE model. We describe the phased development and implementation of ePMA teaching and assessment using the BPS platform. Evaluation was quality improvement in orientation and included structured feedback from students, tutors and assessors; operational metrics including technical reliability, use of paper contingency processes and examiner staffing requirements; and assessment outputs including automated marking data, item-level performance and cohort-level examination observations used to support iterative refinement. RESULTS: Feedback from staff supported the feasibility and acceptability of the approach. Operational data showed low reliance on paper contingencies and reduced examiner requirements (approximately 400 examiner hours annually) for prescribing Objective Structured Clinical Examinations. Automated marking and item-level assessment outputs identified common prescribing errors and informed refinements to subsequent teaching materials. CONCLUSION: This report describes the integration of the BPS platform into teaching and assessment within a large medical programme. Quality-improvement data suggest the approach was feasible to deliver at scale, aligned teaching and assessment closer with clinical practice and the Prescribing Safety Assessment and generated valuable data to support ongoing curriculum development and refinement.

articles.title: Investigating potential prognostic genes and candidate therapeutic targets for acute myeloid leukemia in food-medicine homologous plants via integrated network pharmacology and transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematologic malignancy. Conventional chemotherapy often causes substantial adverse effects, while food-medicine homologous plants with favorable safety profiles and multitarget regulatory activities offer a promising strategy for AML treatment. This study aimed to screen core bioactive compounds from 106 food-medicine homologous plants, identify potential prognostic genes related to AML, and explore the molecular mechanisms of their anti-AML activities. Public omics cohorts for AML were systematically analyzed to screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs). The DEGs were intersected with the target genes of 106 food-medicine homologous plants to obtain candidate genes for subsequent GO/KEGG functional enrichment analysis and PPI network analysis. Core bioactive compounds were screened and prioritized via the Graph-based Bilinear Attention Network (GraphBAN) combined with druggability and toxicology screening criteria. Potential prognostic genes were identified via univariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis and further screening. Immune infiltration analysis and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed on the identified potential prognostic genes. Bioinformatic prediction was conducted to identify upstream transcription factors (TFs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) targeting these genes and to analyze their chromosomal distribution and subcellular localization characteristics. Binding affinity and stability between core active compounds and proteins encoded by potential prognostic genes were systematically confirmed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation analyses. The expression levels of potential prognostic genes were finally validated via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). We identified 1102 candidate genes, 542 core bioactive compounds, and 6 potential prognostic genes. The constructed prognostic model demonstrated moderate predictive performance. Immune infiltration analysis identified 18 types of differentially infiltrated immune-cell populations (P < 0.05), and GSEA results indicated that immunity-related signaling pathways were enriched in the AML high-risk subgroup. Moreover, 138 chemotherapeutic agents were identified. MYB-centered transcription factors and numerous microRNAs were found to regulate these potential prognostic genes. The genes reside on distinct chromosomes; for example, ITGB3 is located on chromosome 17. Further subcellular localization analysis revealed distinct protein distribution patterns. IGF1R, ITGB3, and SLC38A1 are predominantly located on the cell membrane, while KYNU, PDE4A, and GSTM2 are mostly located in the cytoplasm. Molecular docking revealed that the binding energy between IGF1R and MOL008397 was - 10.7 kcal/mol. Molecular dynamics simulation further confirmed the stability of this molecular complex. RT-qPCR verified distinct expression of the six prognostic genes in clinical AML blood samples. This study identified core active compounds and potential prognostic genes against AML derived from food-medicine homologous plants, which provides evidence for prognosis evaluation and targeted therapy.

articles.title: Development and validation of a GC-MS method for the determination of ethylene glycol and diethylene glycol in pharmaceutical syrups.
articles.abstract: Contamination of pharmaceutical syrups with ethylene glycol (EG) and diethylene glycol (DEG) has led to serious poisoning incidents worldwide, highlighting the necessity for strong regulations and reliable testing methods. A gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method was developed and validated in accordance with ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. The method was developed for pharmaceutical syrup matrices and validated using multiple commercially available products, supporting its applicability for routine regulatory surveillance. It exhibited excellent linearity, with r² of 0.9991 for EG and 0.9963 for DEG. The detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) limits were 0.02% v/v and 0.06% v/v, respectively, below the regulatory limit of 0.10% set by the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA), Ministry of Health Malaysia. Accuracy ranged from 94.2% to 108.4%, and the %RSD for intermediate precision was 1.4% for EG and 2.5% for DEG, confirming the method's reproducibility. When the validated method was applied to 51 pharmaceutical syrup samples available in the Malaysian market as part of post-market surveillance, 13 samples were detected to have EG. Of these, 11 samples had EG concentrations between the LOD and the LOQ, while two samples (PS-13 and PS-26) had measurable levels at 0.09% v/v. DEG was not detected in any sample. Therefore, this study emphasises the importance of regulatory surveillance, supported by validated analytical testing, to ensure the quality and safety of pharmaceutical syrups. Strengthening local surveillance mechanisms will further strengthen NPRA's regulatory capacity and safeguard public health.

articles.title: Polymer-based Vaginal Insert Systems: Engineering Controlled Drug Delivery for Women's Health.
articles.abstract: Polymer-based vaginal inserts have emerged as a promising approach for localized and systemic drug delivery, demonstrating improved therapeutic efficacy, prolonged drug residence, controlled release and enhanced patient compliance compared to conventional vaginal dosage forms. This article gives a complete overview of the design and development of polymer-based vaginal inserts, covering the influence of vaginal physiology, mucoadhesion and polymer selection on formulation performance. The properties and applications of natural, synthetic, and hybrid polymers, and current breakthroughs in fabrication technologies such as freeze-drying, solvent casting, hot-melt extrusion, electrospinning, and 3D printing are covered. Also examined are several drug release techniques such as sustained, swelling-controlled, stimuli-responsive and mucoadhesive systems. Moreover, the therapeutic potential of vaginal inserts for the treatment of vulvovaginal infections, endometriosis, cervical cancer, uterine fibroids, menopause-related illnesses, contraception and HIV prevention is emphasized. Finally, the future directions of emerging technologies, such as nanotechnology, smart polymers, artificial intelligence, and personalized drug delivery systems, are discussed for the clinical translation and enhanced efficacy of polymer-based vaginal drug delivery systems for women's reproductive health.

articles.title: Landscape of small molecules derived from marine sources and their clinical progression.
articles.abstract: 1. Marine organisms have fascinated scientists with their unique and unparalleled biodiversity and therapeutic potential.2. They are known to possess novel bioactive compounds with varied pharmacological properties that encompass anticancer, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, antiviral, and cardioprotective properties.3. The review is put forth to discuss key advancements in landscapes of small molecules derived from marine sources, along with their clinical status.4. We also identify key challenges in marine drug discovery, such as access to marine organisms, supply chain sustainability, chemical diversity, synthesis complexity, bioavailability optimization, and intellectual property concerns.4. The review also put forth the discussions on improving the drug discovery area from marine sources by considering the advancements in marine biotechnology, artificial intelligence, and interdisciplinary collaborations.5. Redressing these challenges and adopting emerging technologies, the potential of marine biodiversity may be harnessed for biomedical innovation and, in turn, contribute to health and promote environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Tradipitant for Motion Sickness-A GRADE Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tradipitant, a neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist, for preventing motion sickness-induced vomiting. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through February 2026 without language or date resrictions. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Randomized controlled trials comparing tradipitant (85 or 170 mg) with placebo in adults with motion sickness were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, assessed risk of bias using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, and evaluated certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. DATA SYNTHESIS: Three randomized controlled trials (N = 808) were included. Tradipitant significantly reduced overall vomiting vs placebo (risk ratio [RR], 0.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.30-0.48; I2 = 0%) and improved the composite nausea/vomiting outcome (RR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.35-0.65). Serious adverse events and somnolence were comparable between groups, although fatigue was more frequent with tradipitant (RR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.02-6.93).Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison to Existing Drugs:Unlike antihistamines and anticholinergics, which are frequently limited by sedation and anticholinergic adverse effects, tradipitant significantly reduces motion-induced vomiting with minimal sedation and may benefit patients who do not respond to or cannot tolerate conventional therapies. CONCLUSIONS: Tradipitant significantly reduces motion sickness-induced vomiting while maintaining a favorable safety profile, supporting its role as an effective treatment option pending further comparative studies.

articles.title: Case Report: Pyrrolizidine alkaloid-induced hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome misdiagnosed as ovarian malignancy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic Sinusoidal Obstruction Syndrome (HSOS), formerly known as Hepatic Veno-Occlusive Disease (HVOD), is a rare and life-threatening liver condition. It is often caused by the ingestion of pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs), which are found in plants such as Gynura segetum (Tusanqi). Because its clinical presentation is non-specific, HSOS is frequently misdiagnosed. CASE PRESENTATION: A 72-year-old female with a 5-year history of type 2 diabetes presented with abdominal distension and anorexia for 2 weeks. Initial examinations revealed massive ascites and significantly elevated tumor markers (Cancer Antigen 125(CA125): 195.0 U/mL, Human Epididymis Protein 4(HE4): 120.1 pmol/L). Imaging suggested potential ovarian cancer, leading to diagnostic laparoscopy and bilateral adnexectomy. However, intraoperative findings and post-operative pathology showed no evidence of malignancy, identifying only a serous cystadenoma. Subsequent detailed history-taking revealed long-term ingestion of "Tusanqi." Re-evaluation via contrast-enhanced CT and MRCP showed characteristic patterns: patchy enhancement of hepatic parenchyma ("geographic" pattern), narrow hepatic veins, and signs of portal hypertension. The patient was finally diagnosed with PA-induced HSOS. Following a regimen of anticoagulation (low-molecular-weight heparin), liver protection, and diuretics, the patient's abdominal distension relieved, and liver function markers showed partial recovery. The patient underwent laparoscopic bilateral adnexectomy due to a high suspicion of ovarian cancer, but the postoperative pathology ruled out malignant tumors, resulting in unnecessary surgical trauma. This article aims to improve the warning effect. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the clinical challenge of distinguishing HSOS from abdominal malignancies. A thorough dietary/herbal history and characteristic "geographic" enhancement on imaging are pivotal for avoiding unnecessary surgical interventions.

articles.title: Development of an Injectable Boronic Ester Nanocomposite Hydrogel for pH- and Thermo-Responsive Gentamicin Delivery and Antibacterial Activity.
articles.abstract: Infected wounds require localized antimicrobial treatment strategies that provide sustained drug release, reduce systemic antibiotic exposure, and promote tissue repair. This study reports an infection-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform based on dynamic covalent boronic ester chemistry for triggered topical antibiotic delivery. Phenylboronic acid (PBA)-functionalized cationic nanoparticles (PBA-NPs) were employed as three-dimensional crosslinkers and combined with poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) to construct an injectable nanocomposite hydrogel via reversible boronic ester interactions. The nanocomposite hydrogel was characterized for morphology, injectability, rheological properties, stimuli-responsive behavior, in vitro antibiotic release, and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The resulting nanocomposite hydrogel exhibited a gel-sol transition at 39.7°C, while the pH-dependent chemistry of the boronic ester network supports enhanced network dissociation under mildly acidic conditions (pH 6.5). This dual pH- and thermo-responsive behavior enabled on-demand release of encapsulated gentamicin sulfate while preserving viscoelastic recovery consistent with dynamic network reconstruction. The cationic PBA-NPs exhibited intrinsic antibacterial activity and generated enhanced antimicrobial effects when combined with gentamicin. Zones of inhibition reached 22 mm (S. aureus) and 25 mm (P. aeruginosa) at 3% drug loading. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dynamic covalent boronic ester nanocomposite hydrogel represents a promising injectable platform for infection-responsive localized antibiotic delivery and antibacterial wound management.
