Co-injections of L-NAC methyl ester reduce the loss of antinociception and prevent the occurrence of hyperalgesia elicited by injections of fentanyl in male rats.
articles.abstract: The development of hyperalgesia (i.e., enhanced physical pain and/or psychological distress) during chronic fentanyl use plays a vital role in the continued and accelerated use of this potent synthetic opioid. Numerous biochemical changes in the brain, such as changes in redox status, are thought to contribute to the development of hyperalgesia to fentanyl and other opioids. This study addresses whether the clinically used antioxidant N-acetyl-L-cysteine (L-NAC) and its readily cell-penetrant analogue, L-NAC methyl ester (L-NACme) would affect the progressive loss of antinociception and appearance of hyperalgesia in adult male Sprague Dawley rats. We monitored changes in tail-flick latencies following twice daily co-injections over 5 days (8 AM, 8 PM) of fentanyl (125 μg/kg, IV) + vehicle or L-NAC (500 μmol/kg, IV) or L-NACme (500 μmol/kg, IV) in the rats. The first co-injections of fentanyl + vehicle elicited a long-lasting antinociception, whereas a robust hyperalgesia appeared with co-injections 5 and was even more dramatic following co-injections 6-10. The co-injections of fentanyl + L-NAC partially prevented the loss of antinociception and occurrence of hyperalgesia, and co-injections of fentanyl and L-NACme markedly reduced the loss of antinociception and prevented the appearance of hyperalgesia. This study provides evidence that L-NAC and L-NACme beneficially affect the alterations in pain processing that occurs with sub-chronic administration of fentanyl. The higher efficacy of L-NACme is likely to be due to its greater cell penetrability in brain regions and interaction with intracellular signaling cascades, which may include redox-dependent processes, that mediate fentanyl-induced antinociception and hyperalgesia.

articles.title: Mutagenicity studies on migrants from food-contact silicone products based on Ames test and chemical analysis.
articles.abstract: After simulating food migration using 95% ethanol at 70°C for 2 h on 63 food-contact silicone products, the Ames test was employed to evaluate the mutagenicity of their migrants. Chemical analyses of three positive samples were conducted using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The results indicated that the TA98 strain was more sensitive than the TA97, TA100, and TA102 strains. None of the 30 nipples exhibited mutagenicity against the TA98 strain, whereas 26 of 33 kitchen utensils (79%) tested positive. Migration from a representative sample (K-19, mold) in 95% ethanol demonstrated mutagenicity whether used at room temperature, baked, or frozen, indicating higher mutagenicity when in contact with fatty foods. A total of 22 organic compounds and 14 metal elements were detected in the samples, with migration levels of heavy metals and phthalates below the specific migration limits. The significant difference in results between nipples and kitchenware may be related to differences in their formulations and processing techniques. Further studies are needed to identify the key substances responsible for mutagenicity in these samples and to conduct subsequent risk assessments. Although potentially harmful, these findings do not necessarily indicate a safety risk.

articles.title: Acute atrazine exposure does not impair 5α-reductase activity in hepatic and blood-brain barrier cells.
articles.abstract: Atrazine is a widely used herbicide with non-canonical endocrine-disrupting activity as it does not act as a hormone agonist yet it induces hormone imbalances, represented by induced feminization and heightened aromatase levels. Still, its endocrinological effects remain poorly understood especially in mammalian systems. This study investigated whether atrazine and its two major metabolites (deisopropylatrazine and deethylatrazine) interfere with the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in vitro in two cellular models representing the liver and the blood-brain barrier, the latter being herein reported for the first time. Transcriptional activation of the estrogen receptor was assessed, while potential interactions with steroid 5α-reductase isoforms type I and II were evaluated by molecular docking. Testosterone conversion to dihydrotestosterone was measured in Hep-G2 and bEnd.3 cells after acute exposure to atrazine and its two main metabolites at different concentrations (100nM - 50μM), along with endpoint cellular metabolic activity. Neither atrazine nor its metabolites activated the estrogen receptor and molecular docking predicted weak interactions of atrazine, deisopropylatrazine and deethylatrazine, with both 5α-reductase isoforms compared with testosterone. Consistent with these predictions, no significant decreases in dihydrotestosterone synthesis were observed in either cell line following treatment, both Hep-G2 and bEnd.3 cells lines retaining the unaffected ability of converting testosterone to its more potent form - dihydrotestosterone. These results indicate that atrazine and its major metabolites do not directly impair testosterone conversion to dihydrotestosterone, and that they are unlikely to disrupt androgen conversion through inhibition of 5α-reductase activity, the main anti-androgenic mechanism known to cause heightened aromatase levels.

articles.title: The penetration of the Novichok nerve agent A-234 in a human skin model and the assessment of several decontamination procedures.
articles.abstract: The recent use of a Novichok nerve agent for an assassination attempt on Alexei Navalny underlined the importance of identifying effective countermeasures. The immediate decontamination is essential to reduce the penetration of the chemical agent into the systemic circulation. Only limited data are available about the decontamination of Novichok nerve agents on the skin. In this study, we used an in vitro model of human skin to determine the efficacy of decontaminants to remove the agent A-234. The skin was exposed towards A-234 and after 5min or 30min the decontamination was initiated by applying different decontamination protocols (Reactive Skin Decontamination Lotion (RSDL), the potassium salt of the acetohydroxamic acid (AHAK), sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) 2%, soapy water 2% and tap water). Then, the amount of penetrated A-234 was calculated using an acetylcholinesterase inhibition assay. The early decontamination with AHAK was most effective resulting in a complete decontamination, i.e. 0% residual A-234. In contrast, soapy water, tap water, RSDL and NaOCl showed a lower decontamination efficacy and the penetrated amount of A-234 was reduced by 89% (soapy water, tap water), 91% (RSDL) and 95% (NaOCl). The delayed decontamination after 30min also revealed a complete decontamination of A-234 by using AHAK and an inadequate decontamination using soapy water, tap water, RSDL and NaOCl. In conclusion, the results underline that the decontamination of the Novichok agent A-234 was similar to the V-series nerve agent VX. The relatively new AHAK was a promising decontaminant and deserves further investigation.

articles.title: Identification of predisposing factors for hematotoxicity in occupational benzene-exposed workers using machine learning and SHAP interpretation.
articles.abstract: Benzene is an important industrial material and environmental pollutant, and even low-level exposure has been associated with hematotoxicity. Therefore, the identification of predisposing factors for hematotoxicity induced by occupational benzene exposure is crucial for managing occupational benzene poisoning. Herein, we recruited 1513 petrochemical workers in southern China, including 847 control workers and 666 workers with hematotoxicity. After randomly dividing the dataset into a training set (75%) and a test set (25%), we employed six machine learning algorithms construct a prediction model. Through recursive feature elimination, 22 feature variables, including age, work years, department, benzene, toluene, xylene, noise, AST/ALT, ALP, GGT, TBIL, DBIL, TC, TG, LDL-C, HDL-C, GLU, SCr, Urea, UA, FEV1/FVC%, and DBP were initially identified. Styrene was included due to its occupational relevance, resulting in 23 input variables for model development. We found the XGBoost algorithm was the optimal model for identifying factors affecting hematotoxicity. SHAP analysis based on the XGBoost model further characterized the contributions of variables at both the overall and individual levels, identifying benzene, noise, work years, age, department, and liver function indicators as important factors while also showing the direction and magnitude of their associations with the predicted risk of hematotoxicity. In vitro experiments also shown that impaired liver function exacerbated 4-benzoquinone (1,4-BQ)-induced cytotoxicity in bone marrow cells and modulated the underlying molecular pathways. Together, liver function-related indicators emerged as important predictors of hematotoxicity risk among benzene-exposed workers. These findings may help inform occupational health surveillance and risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Early-Life Minocycline Exposure Produces Sustained Redox Modulation but Persistent Locomotor Deficits in Drosophila melanogaster.
articles.abstract: 1. Minocycline has shown therapeutic potential in neurodegeneration and ageing, but the effects of exposure during development remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether minocycline exposure restricted to development alters redox status and locomotor function in adult Drosophila melanogaster after drug withdrawal.2. A preliminary adult survival assay was used to inform dose selection. Fly eggs were cultured on standard food containing minocycline at 0.05, 0.10 or 0.20 mM from embryonic development through eclosion. Adults were then transferred to untreated food and assessed on post-eclosion day 5. Larval feeding and body-wall contraction were assessed as developmental behavioural endpoints, adult climbing performance was assessed using the negative geotaxis assay, and redox status was evaluated using FOX-reactive peroxides, nitric oxide-related measures, thiols and malondialdehyde.3. Developmental minocycline exposure reduced FOX-reactive peroxide and nitric oxide-related measures and increased thiol levels in adults. Exposure also impaired larval feeding and adult climbing performance, whereas pupation and larval crawling were not significantly altered.4. Developmental minocycline exposure was associated with altered redox status and locomotor deficits that remained evident in early adulthood following drug withdrawal. These findings support further investigation of the tissue-specific and molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of developmental minocycline exposure.

articles.title: Longitudinal Modeling of Cardiometabolic Dysfunction in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Using Item Response Theory.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic dysfunction in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) is reflected by multiple risk factors and cannot be fully characterized by any single biomarker. Item response theory (IRT) provides a framework for integrating observed risk factors into latent measures of underlying cardiometabolic dysfunction. Routinely collected measurements of systolic and diastolic blood pressure (sBP and dBP), high- and low-density lipoproteins (HDL and LDL), triglycerides (TG), HbA1c, and BMI from 33,396 adults newly diagnosed with T2D were analyzed, with biomarkers categorized into four ordered levels. A two-dimensional model described the data better than a unidimensional, identifying a blood pressure-related latent variable ( ψ  1) primarily informed by sBP and dBP, and a metabolic latent variable ( ψ  2) primarily informed by HDL, HbA1c, TG, and BMI, while LDL showed low discrimination on both dimensions. At baseline, age at T2D diagnosis was associated with both latent variables, with opposing effects of 0.02 for ψ  1 and -0.07 for ψ  2. Sex was associated with ψ  2, with women scoring 0.43 units lower than men on the latent variable scale. Longitudinally, ψ  1 and ψ  2 showed post-baseline offsets of -0.10 and -0.22, respectively, followed by separately estimated annual slopes of approximately -0.03 year-1. HbA1c exhibited a distinct trajectory with an initial post-baseline improvement followed by deterioration, requiring an item-specific slope of 0.45 year-1. The ψ  2 contributed modest additional information for all-cause mortality beyond age and sex. This framework integrated routinely collected biomarkers into continuous latent measures of multidimensional cardiometabolic dysfunction while accounting for differences in their contributions to the latent dimensions.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics of Metoprolol in Cisgender Males, Cisgender Females, and Transgender Women Receiving Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: 1. This exploratory pilot study aimed to characterize metoprolol pharmacokinetics and assess the feasibility of pharmacokinetic sampling among cisgender males, cisgender females, and transgender women receiving gender-affirming hormone therapy.2. Nine healthy volunteers (three per group) received a single 100 mg oral dose of metoprolol, and serial blood samples were collected over 12 hours. Plasma metoprolol concentrations were determined using HPLC and analyzed by a non-compartment model. CYP2D6 genotyping or phenotyping was not performed; therefore, the analysis was descriptive and hypothesis-generating.3. Descriptively, mean area under the concentration-time curve values were 2550 ± 126 ng·h/mL in cisgender males, 2142 ± 463 ng·h/mL in cisgender females, and 1522 ± 189 ng·h/mL in transgender participants. Mean peak plasma concentrations were 418 ± 43, 363 ± 58, and 269 ± 27 ng/mL, respectively. The corresponding elimination rates were 0.139, 0.140, and 0.268 h-1, and mean half-lives were 4.98, 4.92, and 2.58 h, respectively.4. The observed profiles suggest between-participant variability that warrants further investigation; however, three participants per group cannot represent the respective populations, and the findings cannot be attributed to sex, gender, or hormone therapy without CYP2D6 genotype data. Larger, genotype-stratified studies with detailed hormone and body-composition measurements are required.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-Based Oral Delivery of Capecitabine: In Vitro Cytotoxicity and Pharmacokinetic Evaluation in HepG2 and HT-29 Cell Lines.
articles.abstract: Present study aims to develop and assess a capecitabine-loaded nanoparticle formulation (C18) for improved oral bioavailability and targeted anticancer activity.Capecitabine nanoparticles were successfully prepared using a double emulsion solvent evaporation process. These nanoparticles were then tested for in vitro cytotoxicity using MTT assays against HT-29, HepG2 and L929 cell lines to calculate IC50 values. The pharmacokinetic properties of the medication and its nanoparticle formulation were also investigated in Wistar rats after oral administration. Validated HPLC methods were used to assess the plasma concentrations of 5-FU and capecitabine, and data was processed using PkSolver software.The nanoparticle formulation (C18) exhibited dose-dependent cytotoxicity by IC50 values of 38.91 µg/mL (HepG2) and 55.15 µg/mL (HT-29), showing superior anticancer activity compared to 5-FU. Cytotoxicity toward normal L929 cells was moderate, indicating selective toxicity. Pharmacokinetic studies revealed enhanced oral bioavailability, increased Cmax and AUC, and prolonged circulation time for the nanoparticle formulation compared to the conventional drug.Capecitabine-loaded nanoparticles demonstrated improved cytotoxic potential against cancer cell lines and favorable pharmacokinetic profiles, associate their probability as an active oral nanocarrier system for cancer therapy.

articles.title: GLS2 reshapes glycolytic metabolism and bioenergetic homeostasis in glioblastoma cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits extensive metabolic reprogramming, including glucose and glutamine (Gln) addiction, with Gln being converted into glutamate by glutaminase, encoded by the GLS and GLS2 genes. GLS2 acts as a context-dependent tumor suppressor, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. GLS2 is silenced in GBM, and we previously showed that its re-expression modulates pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) activity and tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCAC) metabolism, suggesting a distinct metabolic rewiring associated with its tumor-suppressive function. METHODS: LN229 and T98G GBM cell lines were used as experimental models. Metabolomic profiling by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was performed to compare changes in central metabolic pathways following GLS2 or GLS overexpression. Glutaminase and PDH enzymatic activities were measured, and Western blotting was performed to assess GLS, GLS2, and PDHA1 protein levels and PDHA1 phosphorylation. A Seahorse analyzer was employed to quantify real-time ATP production derived from glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. RESULTS: Overexpression of GLS2, but not GLS, in LN229 cells caused the accumulation of TCAC-related metabolites, except for citrate, whose depletion is attributed to GLS2's effect on PDH phosphorylation, causing reduced PDH activity. This was accompanied by decreased levels of several acyl-carnitines. Furthermore, GLS2 induced the accumulation of glucose/fructose, while reducing levels of glucose-6-phosphate and pentose-phosphates, consistent with altered glycolysis. GLS2 also diminished the ATP/AMP ratio, confirmed by a reduced ATP synthesis rate, particularly glycolytic ATP, whereas mitochondrial ATP production remained unaltered. CONCLUSIONS: GLS2 exerts an isoenzyme-specific effect on Gln and glucose metabolism in GBM, likely modulating the glycolysis/pentose-phosphate pathway (PPP)-TCAC-axis.
